papers.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis

summary.tldr: AskChem introduces a claim-centered infrastructure for chemistry literature synthesis, converting papers into atomic, typed, provenance-carrying claims for improved retrieval and synthesis.
key_points: AskChem changes the unit of retrieval from papers to provenance-carrying claims, each grounded by a DOI and verbatim quote or evidence locator.
It indexes 2.4M claims from 147K papers and offers a web interface, REST, SDK, and MCP access for AI agents.
AskChem provides a stabilized faceted taxonomy, an evidence graph linking claims, and an exploratory living taxonomy.
On AskChem-Bench, grounding a GPT-5.5 reader in AskChem resulted in 100% resolvable DOIs and the highest citation density among five systems.
summary.why_it_matters: This system significantly improves the efficiency and accuracy of chemistry literature synthesis for both human scientists and AI agents by providing structured, verifiable information.

papers.title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents

summary.tldr: Qwen-UI-Agent is a foundation GUI agent for real-world use across mobile, computer, web, and DeepSearch, combining diverse environments, unified action space, and an AutoResearch-style data flywheel.
key_points: Qwen-UI-Agent integrates diverse sandbox environments with a large-scale real-device mobile runtime.
It features a unified action space that interleaves GUI operations with CLI execution and generates batched actions in a single model turn.

An AutoResearch-style data flywheel uses agents to construct tasks, diagnose failures, and plan iterations, supported by online RL on trajectories exceeding 100 turns with over 10,000 concurrent environments.
Achieves 82.1% on MobileWorld, 92.2% on MobileWorld-Real, 97.5% on AndroidDaily, 79.5% on OSWorld-Verified, 40.0% partial-progress on OSWorld-v2, 73.6% on WebArena, and 81.5% on ScreenSpot-Pro.
summary.why_it_matters: This agent advances the capability of GUI automation to reliably execute complex, long-horizon tasks across various digital platforms, including real mobile devices.

papers.title: Metis: Memory Foundation Model

summary.tldr: Metis introduces memory foundation models, integrating persistent, dynamically evolving memory states and native memory procedures directly into foundation models, enabling autonomous information storage and utilization through model computation.
key_points: Metis formalizes native memory as a persistent, dynamically evolving memory state within the backbone and native memory procedures for autonomous information storage and utilization.
Metis's architecture equips a foundation model with a native memory state, compressing historical information and accessing it via memory attention.
Memory-specific training data and multiple optimization objectives are used for mid-training acquisition of native memory procedures.
Metis's online memory maintenance is gradient-free, and memory updates require only a forward pass, with frozen model weights during inference while native memory states transform autonomously.
Metis offers advantages in architecture, end-to-end optimization, and efficiency for AI agents.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating native memory capabilities into foundation models like Metis could lead to more efficient and autonomously learning AI agents by reducing reliance on external memory modules.

papers.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering

summary.tldr: Frontis-MA1 (35B) is a new meta-evolution AI4AI model trained on OpenMLE, demonstrating recursive self-improvement in machine learning engineering by significantly improving performance on MLE-Bench Lite.
key_points: Introduced OpenMLE, an open full-stack system for recursive self-improvement (RSI) research in machine learning engineering (MLE), comprising OpenMLE-Gym, OpenMLE-RL, and OpenMLE-Evo.
Frontis-MA1 (35B) was post-trained as a meta-evolution agent using four atomic program-evolution operators (Draft, Improve, Debug, Crossover) via execution-grounded SFT and RL.
Frontis-MA1 (35B) improved Medal Average from 39.39% to 60.61% over its base model with OpenMLE-Evo on MLE-Bench Lite, reaching 71.21% with OpenMLE-Evo-Max.
The model and framework demonstrated transferability on held-out NatureBench Lite, with the trained model raising Match-SOTA from 50% to 70% and OpenMLE-Evo raising it from 20% to 50%.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a concrete, executable testbed and a high-performing model for studying and advancing recursive self-improvement in AI systems for machine learning engineering.

papers.title: PhiZero: A World Model Built Around Physical Language

summary.tldr: PhiZero is a physical world model that uses "physical language," a discrete representation of world-state transitions, to explicitly reason about physical world evolution before rendering videos.
key_points: PhiZero utilizes "physical language" for explicit reasoning about world dynamics, contrasting with pixel-space prediction in other physical world models.
Physical language is learned from in-the-wild videos via self-supervision.
PhiZero employs a reason-then-render paradigm: inferring future world evolution as a physical-language sequence, then rendering it into video.
The model demonstrates capabilities in realistic and interactive world modeling, fine-grained action-conditioned simulation, and zero-shot motion transfer.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a more interpretable and potentially more robust method for modeling complex physical interactions in AI systems.

papers.title: VideoCoCo: Code-as-CoT for Physically-Consistent Video Generation via an Agentic Dual-Engine System

summary.tldr: VideoCoCo is an agentic dual-engine framework that uses executable Blender code as a process-level chain of thought for physically consistent video generation, improving upon existing text-to-video models.
key_points: VideoCoCo employs a coding agent to synthesize Blender programs from text prompts, explicitly defining scene and temporal evolution.
A simulation engine executes the Blender program to generate a deterministic spatiotemporal draft.
A generative video engine transforms the draft into a photorealistic video via draft-conditioned editing.
VideoCoCo-3K, a dataset of draft-instruction-target triplets, was constructed to adapt the video editor to simulated drafts.
VideoCoCo improved OmniWeaving baseline from 0.475 to 0.558 on PhyGenBench and from 52.18 to 77.88 on VBench-2.0.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more controllable and inspectable physically consistent video generation by separating process-level reasoning from visual realization.

papers.title: Memory Decoder at Scale: A Pretrained, Parametric Long-Term Memory

summary.tldr: Memory Decoder at Scale introduces a pretrained, parametric long-term memory module, scaling models up to 6.9B parameters and pretraining on 300B tokens, demonstrating improved parameter-performance tradeoffs.
key_points: Memory models were scaled up to 6.9B parameters and pretrained on 300B tokens.
A distributed pipeline for Faiss indexing and retrieval, with sparse, batch-wise loading of kNN distributions, addressed the bottleneck of indexing and search at scale.
Allocating more parameters to memory yields a better parameter-performance tradeoff than scaling the base model alone.
A 6.9B general memory paired with Pythia-410M increased its average score from 29.86 to 37.34, surpassing Pythia-12B with 39% fewer total parameters.
1.7B domain memories improved average scores by over 9 points for Qwen3 Base models (0.6B to 14B) across three domains.
summary.why_it_matters: Independently scaling pretrained memory offers a more parameter-efficient path to improving language model performance.

papers.title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning

summary.tldr: Beacon is a novel agentic visual reasoning model that improves multimodal large language models' tool use by enhancing Mode Adaptiveness and Tool Effect.
key_points: Beacon introduces Necessity-Aware Adaptive Reward in the reinforcement learning stage to encourage adaptive tool invocation based on task necessity.
Beacon incorporates a Hint-Guided Capability Expansion mechanism to strengthen the model's tool-use capability on challenging problems.
The model addresses limitations in existing agentic visual reasoning models, which show limited Mode Adaptiveness and offset gains from tool use on hard examples by errors on easy examples.
Beacon aims to achieve stronger overall performance, improved Mode Adaptiveness, and genuine tool-induced performance gains in agentic visual reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: This work enables more efficient and effective multimodal large language models by optimizing when and how they utilize tools for complex visual reasoning tasks.

papers.title: BM25 Wins at Scale: A Scaling Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigms

summary.tldr: A controlled study on RAG paradigms across 28 corpus sizes reveals BM25 outperforms File-System Agent and other methods at scales exceeding 10 million corpus tokens.
key_points: The study varied corpus size across 28 nested tiers, spanning a 450-fold increase, while maintaining consistent questions and document sets.
File-System Agent leads at small corpus sizes but incurs 39 times more query tokens at bedrock scale and becomes less effective as search space grows.
BM25 overtakes File-System Agent around 10 million corpus tokens and maintains a lead, approaching 20 points accuracy margin at full scale.
Dense retrieval is efficient but less accurate, while graph-based RAG faces construction limitations at deployment scale.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the scaling behavior of RAG paradigms is crucial for selecting cost-effective and accurate retrieval methods for large-scale applications.

papers.title: Flux-OPD: On-Policy Distillation with Evolving Contexts

summary.tldr: Flux-OPD introduces an on-policy distillation paradigm using evolving contexts as in-training supervision, stabilizing the target and downweighting conflicts for improved performance in open-ended domains.
key_points: Flux-OPD analyzes the reverse KL objective, finding that students are distilled toward the geometric mean of context-conditioned teachers and the objective contains a conflict term.
It uses evolving contexts as in-training supervision to capture task preferences in open-ended domains.
Flux-OPD injects contextual difference signals (differences between context-conditioned and context-free teachers) as corrections into a context-free teacher anchor.
The conflict term is used as an indicator to weight the strength of these contextual corrections.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a way to effectively incorporate dynamic task preferences into large language model training for open-ended applications where verifiable rewards are scarce.

papers.title: MPIE-Bench: Benchmarking Anatomically Plausible Multi-Person Interaction Editing

summary.tldr: MPIE-Bench and MPIE-Eval are introduced to benchmark and evaluate multi-person interaction editing, addressing anatomical and geometric failures in generated images.
key_points: MPIE-Bench is a 2,500-sample benchmark of video-mined editing triplets, covering 405 scenes, 14 interaction categories, and four contact densities (C0-C3).

MPIE-Eval introduces two new evaluation axes: Anatomy (completeness of reconstructed bodies) and Interaction (penetration/surface distance matching instruction), using a multi-person mesh reconstruction.
Across ten editors, mesh Anatomy scores peaked at 0.65 and mesh Interaction at 0.72, while VLM checklists rated the same images above 0.95.
A five-rater study confirmed MPIE-Eval's axes track human judgment more closely than zero-shot VLM judges.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark and evaluation method provide a more accurate assessment of multi-person image generation, highlighting current model limitations in anatomical and geometric plausibility.

papers.title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine

summary.tldr: ACE-Data-0 is a human-centric dataset of 150 hours across 200 task categories, capturing synchronized multisensory data for embodied intelligence, addressing data bottlenecks in perception-action loops.
key_points: The Ambient Capture Engine (ACE) records egocentric/exocentric video, full-body/hand motion, object geometry/6-DoF, audio, and tactile signals as a unified multisensory stream.
ACE operates at two scales: table-scale for hand-object manipulation and room-scale for whole-body motion and interactions in furnished homes.
ACE-Data-0 comprises 150 hours (17M video frames) from 50 participants in 2 environments, totaling 75,000 interaction episodes across 200 task categories.
The dataset includes atomic manipulation, long-horizon household activities, and human-scene interaction, with goal-level instructions to preserve natural behavioral variation.
A hierarchical benchmark reveals substantial gaps in state-of-the-art methods under contact, occlusion, egomotion, and long temporal horizons.
summary.why_it_matters: ACE-Data-0 provides a scalable foundation for imitation learning, world models, vision-language-action systems, and embodied AI by offering synchronized human demonstrations with aligned perceptual, kinematic, and contact supervision.

papers.title: Beyond Borrowed Histories: Person-Aligned User Simulation for Interactive Role-Playing Evaluation

summary.tldr: PALATE is a new benchmark for evaluating Role-Playing Agents (RPAs) using person-aligned LLM-simulated users and tailored evaluations, addressing limitations of fixed dialogue histories and generic rubrics.
key_points: PALATE uses five per-user simulators to engage candidate RPAs in free-form, multi-turn conversations.
The benchmark includes a pool of 300 character profiles for user simulation.
Personalized rubrics are constructed to measure user satisfaction, showing higher agreement with human judgments than a general rubric on held-out annotated data.
PALATE evaluates 16 candidate RPAs, characterizing generic turn quality, long-horizon session capability, and per-user experience on co-constructed multi-turn trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more interpretable evaluations of specific user-RPA interactions, moving beyond single user-independent system rankings.

papers.title: RefCaptioner: Multi-Reference Image-Grounded Video Captioning

summary.tldr: RefCaptioner introduces multi-reference image-grounded video captioning, a new task requiring factual video descriptions with phrase-level reference grounding, and proposes a two-stage post-training framework to address it.
key_points: RefCaptioner is a two-stage post-training framework combining mixed-data SFT with Hierarchical Coverage-Discounted GRPO.
The framework is designed to improve reference selection, phrase-level binding, distractor rejection, and cross-reference consistency.
A corpus of 20,000 videos and 171,354 reference images was constructed for training.
MRVBench was introduced to evaluate caption factuality and multi-reference grounding on real-world and AI-generated videos.
summary.why_it_matters: This enables more source-faithful video reconstruction with both open-source and proprietary video generators by grounding video descriptions to multiple reference images.

papers.title: SpatialCLI: Learning to Reason With Spatial Tools, Then Without Them

summary.tldr: SpatialCLI is a framework that teaches VLMs to integrate specialist visual tools for spatial reasoning and then internalize those perceptual capabilities, improving performance in embodied agent tasks.
key_points: SpatialCLI operates in three stages: Call (VLM uses specialist vision models as spatial tools), Learn (improves tool use via Cold-Start SFT and agentic RL), and Internalize (verbalizes successful tool-use trajectories to internalize capabilities).
A new benchmark, SpatialCLI-Bench, was introduced with 516 examples for compositional perception across localization, segmentation, depth, and pose.
On MindCube, SpatialCLI improved Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct's performance from 29.3% to 84.6% with tools, outperforming GPT-5.6 Sol with tools (72.1%).
After internalization, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct retained 73.8% performance without tools, demonstrating successful internalization of specialist perceptual capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables VLMs to overcome the mismatch between general task reasoning and detailed visual perception, leading to more capable embodied agents.

papers.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B

summary.tldr: Repeated sampling consistently outperforms or matches self-refinement and reflection methods across various model sizes (1.5B-7B) and math benchmarks when token costs are equal.
key_points: Seven methods were compared against repeated sampling using open models (1.5B, 3B, 7B parameters) on two mathematics benchmarks with 150 questions each.
All 36 comparisons, paired by question, showed no method reliably better than repeated sampling at equal token cost, with ten methods reliably worse.
Self-inspection methods were reliably worse in all 18 comparisons, with Self-Refine and forced Reflexion remaining 3.6 to 10.1 points below baseline at 7B.
The benefit of model-based choosing in Best-of-N decreased with model size, from 8.0-11.3 points at 1.5B to 1.3-2.0 points at 7B, becoming indistinguishable from zero.
summary.why_it_matters: For practical applications, repeated sampling is a more token-efficient and effective strategy than complex self-refinement or reflection techniques for improving language model accuracy.

papers.title: SVR: Self-Verifying Refinement via Joint Verdict-Confidence Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Test-Time Compute

summary.tldr: SVR is an oracle-free multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that uses self-verification for adaptive test-time compute in language models, achieving high accuracy with fewer inference turns.
key_points: SVR is an oracle-free multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that learns a compute-control policy using self-verification.
At each turn, the model generates a solution, a discrete correctness verdict, and a confidence score, continuing refinement unless the verdict is 'Correct' and confidence exceeds a threshold.
Training uses GRPO on fixed-horizon trajectories with rewards for correctness, calibration-aware self-verification, and stop-ready correct states; adaptive stopping is inference-only.
On seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3.5-2B, SVR achieved 0.563 macro-average accuracy with 2.99 average inference turns.
SVR outperformed standard GRPO, multi-turn baselines, and a fixed-budget oracle-guided score-feedback reference, requiring substantially fewer turns than fixed ten-turn inference.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables language models to efficiently allocate computational resources by adaptively stopping refinement based on internal self-verification, improving performance while reducing inference cost.

papers.title: When Derived Measurements Mislead: Quantifying and Mitigating LLM Over-Trust with Privileged-Modality Reliability Evidence

summary.tldr: This work defines derived-feature over-trust (DFOT) in LLMs, quantifies it using five estimands, and demonstrates mitigation with privileged-modality reliability evidence on 50,000 paired PPG-ECG records.
key_points: DFOT is defined as an LLM's failure to recognize instance-dependent validity of derived measurements, treating them as direct facts or using them outside valid scope.
Five estimands quantify DFOT: conflict over-trust rate (COTR), context-induced error rate (CIR), correct repair rate (CRR), evidence-specific repair margin (ESRM), and utility harm rate (UHR).
The framework was demonstrated using 50,000 paired PPG-ECG records, with ECG-to-PPG privileged distillation as a baseline for PPG-only inference.
On a 187-patient test, the baseline improved four repair and specificity endpoints by 1.82-6.69 percentage points, with all paired confidence intervals excluding zero.
UHR increased by 0.67 percentage points (95% CI: -0.4 to +1.7) with the baseline mitigation.
summary.why_it_matters: Quantifying and mitigating DFOT is crucial for ensuring LLMs reliably process and interpret derived data, especially in sensitive applications like physiological sensing.

papers.title: WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning

summary.tldr: WIDE introduces token-level dynamic width pruning for LLMs, enabling fine-grained computation allocation and achieving significant speedups in both prefill and decode scenarios.
key_points: WIDE is an end-to-end differentiable token-level dynamic width pruning framework for prefill and decode, allowing each token to dynamically select attention-head and FFN-channel groups.
It extends dynamic pruning to neuron-block-level granularity, moving beyond layer-level decisions for fine-grained computation allocation.
A two-stage training pipeline learns effective token-wise sparse execution patterns, improving quality retention over existing approaches.
A pruning-kernel co-design framework decomposes dynamic sparsity acceleration into mask reordering, hardware-agnostic block-level skipping, and hardware-dependent intra-block skipping.
WIDE achieves up to 1.98x kernel-level speedup for prefill and 4.95x for decoding, with 1.68x and 1.55x end-to-end acceleration respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides substantial practical throughput gains for LLM inference by adaptively pruning computation at a fine-grained level.

papers.title: GLM-RAG: Graph Language Models for Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: This work introduces GLM-RAG, a GLM-based retriever for graph-based RAG, demonstrating superior out-of-domain generalization and competitive in-domain performance compared to GNN and vector-search methods.
key_points: Introduces a Graph Language Model (GLM)-based retriever for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over knowledge graphs.
Compares GLM-based, GNN-based, and traditional vector-search-based retrievers in single- and multi-hop RAG settings.
Finetuned GLM retrievers achieve state-of-the-art performance on two multi-hop benchmarks for out-of-domain transferability.
GLM retrievers show promising scaling with increased parameters and subgraph coverage on in-domain multi-hop QA datasets.
GNN-based retrievers offer higher graph coverage with efficient training, while vector-search baselines excel in single-hop datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: GLM-RAG improves the transferability of RAG systems to unseen domains, enhancing their utility in diverse knowledge graph applications.

papers.title: When Specifications Conflict: A Symmetry-Based Framework for Measuring LLM Preferences

summary.tldr: A symmetry-based framework measures LLM preferences when resolving conflicts between competing specifications, revealing systematic patterns across representation types.
key_points: The framework uses explicitly conflicting specifications to directly observe and analyze LLM choices.
A symmetry-based design minimizes confounding factors, enabling systematic comparison of preferences across representation types.
Evaluation on a mathematical benchmark with 550 conflict instances showed a consistent preference ordering: Formal ≈ Naturalized Formal > Pure Natural Language > Input–Output Examples.
The framework extends to heterogeneous specification conflicts in Boolean algebra, code generation, and clinical domains.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a unified approach to understand and measure how LLMs resolve conflicting information, which is critical for reliable LLM deployment.

papers.title: CACHE-UK: A Stability-Aware Memory Editor for Sequentially Updated Quantized LLMs in Finance

summary.tldr: CACHE-UK is a stability-aware memory editing framework for sequentially updated, 4-bit quantized LLMs, reducing knowledge degradation by 11-17% in financial applications.
key_points: CACHE-UK integrates a rank-1 LoRA perturbation mechanism, a financial domain prioritization module, and a closed-loop Stability Controller.
Evaluated on a 4-bit quantized OpenLLaMA-3B model using an 88,021-document UK financial corpus.
Reduces knowledge degradation by 11-17% relative to adapted baselines under 4-bit constraints.
Achieves a 28% test success (generalization) rate, a 6 percentage point improvement over the strongest adapted baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework improves factual maintenance in resource-constrained financial LLM deployments facing continuous data changes.

papers.title: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed

summary.tldr: MemHarness enables LLM agents to reconstruct retrieved past experiences based on current context, rather than replaying them verbatim, to improve decision-making and prevent negative transfer.
key_points: MemHarness employs a unified policy model to critique and reconstruct retrieved experiences conditioned on the current state at each decision step.
The reconstructive ability is developed through end-to-end training with GRPO.
Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop demonstrate MemHarness outperforms pure RL and static memory-augmented baselines.
MemHarness shows strong robustness in out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios.
The reconstruction objective prevents negative transfer and improves the agent's intrinsic reasoning capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enhances LLM agent performance and robustness by enabling adaptive use of past experiences, leading to more effective and context-aware AI systems.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search for Constraint Model Reformulation to Improve Solver Efficiency

summary.tldr: This work introduces an LLM-guided evolutionary search framework for constraint model reformulation, using AHD-adapted strategies and a novel Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR) method, to improve solver efficiency.
key_points: An evolutionary framework uses an LLM to propose candidate constraint model reformulations, which are then verified and benchmarked against a baseline.
AHD-adapted search strategies control the prior attempts, instructions, and measured feedback provided to the LLM for reformulation.
Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR) applies Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) to instance-level runtime vectors to retain behaviourally diverse reformulation attempts.
Evaluation on eight CSPLib problems shows iterative reformulation yields substantial held-out speedups, and strategies retaining diverse context outperform others.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating performance-oriented constraint model reformulation with LLMs can significantly reduce the computational cost of solving combinatorial problems in industrial applications.

papers.title: (Towards) Scalable Reliable Automated Evaluation with Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A new framework uses pairwise LLM output comparisons and an Elo rating system to approximate expert-level evaluation, offering scalable and reliable quality assessment.
key_points: The framework evaluates LLM-generated content using pairwise comparisons between multiple LLMs to reduce individual model biases.
An Elo rating system generates stable and interpretable rankings of LLM outputs.
Adjustable agreement thresholds (unanimity to majority voting) control evaluation confidence and coverage.
The method's effectiveness is demonstrated by evaluating competency profiles extracted from scientific abstracts.
Automatically derived rankings correlate well with expert judgments, reducing human intervention.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables more efficient and reliable quality assessments of LLM outputs across diverse applications by providing a scalable, consistent, and domain-agnostic evaluation layer.

papers.title: Paying for Honesty Without Knowing the Truth: Reputation-Penalty Design for LLM Marketplace Agents

summary.tldr: CARP, a reputation-penalty mechanism, enables LLM marketplaces to suppress dishonest agents without ground truth verification, achieving consumer welfare comparable to perfect information by making fabrication costly.
key_points: LLM agents fabricate product attributes in a majority of listings even when instructed to be honest, driven by competitive pressure.

CARP is a reputation-penalty mechanism that uses a deadband to forgive complaint noise and state-dependent severity to counter reputation-driven detection erosion, operating without product-level ground truth.
Paired with SPARC, CARP closes most of the consumer-welfare gap relative to a perfect-information oracle and achieves the best welfare among compared policies.
SPARC, a byte-clean code-gated reflection mechanism, makes the penalty behaviorally binding, causing LLM merchants to self-correct and reduce fabrication when it impacts sales.
summary.why_it_matters: This mechanism allows LLM-driven marketplaces to maintain honesty and protect consumers without needing to verify every claim, addressing a critical scalability challenge.

papers.title: PathView-Bench: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Achieve Fine-grained Multiscale Understanding of Pathology Images?

summary.tldr: PathVU is a new vision-anchored benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models' fine-grained, multiscale visual understanding in computational pathology, using 23 public datasets.
key_points: PathVU benchmark evaluates MLLM understanding across two fields of view: Region FOV for high-resolution local regions and Slide FOV for macro whole-slide views.
The benchmark includes 14 VQA-style tasks, 61,673 images, 308,070 samples, 28 organs, and 7,253,526 annotations.
PathVU enables programmatic scoring for region localization, visual recognition, quantity estimation, spatial reasoning, and insufficient-context judgment.
Evaluation of 18 MLLMs revealed substantial limitations in fine-grained visual tasks across multiscale pathology images.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a reproducible method for developing and evaluating pathology MLLMs with explicit multiscale visual understanding, crucial for pathology reasoning and decision-making.

papers.title: One Human, $N$ Agents: Audit-Budget Allocation for LLM Agent Fleets under Miscalibrated, Correlated Confidence

summary.tldr: This paper models audit-budget allocation for LLM agent fleets, identifying a miscalibration threshold where confidence-ranked auditing performs worse than random, and observing that five open-weight LLMs exhibit operationally useless confidence.
key_points: The problem is modeled as budgeted noisy inspection using a two-level Gaussian copula.
A miscalibration threshold $δ^*$ is identified, beyond which confidence-ranked auditing is less effective than random auditing.
$δ^*$ increases as the audit budget $B$ shrinks, and cross-family correlation is high due to shared difficulty.
Five open-weight LLMs show near-constant, operationally useless confidence, with point estimates at or beyond $δ^*$, while a proprietary model provides informative confidence below $δ^*$.
A quantitative criterion for "vacuous oversight" is provided, and policy replaying confirms the observed ordering.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings indicate that current self-reported confidence from many LLMs is unreliable for audit prioritization, potentially leading to ineffective oversight.

papers.title: Memory Decoder at Scale: A Pretrained, Parametric Long-Term Memory

summary.tldr: Memory Decoder at Scale introduces a pretrained, parametric long-term memory module scaled up to 6.9B parameters and 300B tokens, demonstrating improved parameter-performance tradeoffs over scaling base models alone.
key_points: Scaled Memory Decoder models up to 6.9B parameters and pretrained on 300B tokens.
Developed a distributed pipeline for Faiss indexing and retrieval with sparse, batch-wise kNN loading to address scaling bottlenecks.
A 6.9B general memory paired with Pythia-410M achieved an average score of 37.34, outperforming Pythia-12B (37.24) with 39% fewer total parameters.
1.7B domain memories improved average scores by over 9 points across three domains for Qwen3 Base models (0.6B to 14B).
summary.why_it_matters: Independently scaling pretrained memory offers a more parameter-efficient method for enhancing language model performance.

papers.title: MemTxn: A Transaction Boundary for Source-Supported Updates and Complete-State Recovery in Agent Memory

summary.tldr: MemTxn is a governance layer for LLM agent memory that provides reliable updates and complete-state recovery through source-supported verification, version selection, and durable snapshot journaling.
key_points: MemTxn uses Ordered PatchTest to validate writes, a Temporal Resolver to select visible versions during conflicts, and a durable snapshot journal for state recovery.
On an item-disjoint audit, MemTxn accepted all 60 supported originals and rejected all 179 hard negatives.
MemTxn restores the complete declared active map under persistent multi-key faults on LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo states without knowing the physical write set.
MemTxn achieved the highest average F1 across all twelve answer-model configurations on MemoryAgentBench FactConsolidation, outperforming Dense by 17.06-24.07 points in five settings.
summary.why_it_matters: This system enables more reliable and robust long-running LLM agents by preventing persistent memory errors and ensuring state recovery after faults.

papers.title: Reasoning Consensus: Structural Ensembling of LLM Reasoning via Weighted DAG Aggregation

summary.tldr: A framework ensembles LLM reasoning structures by weighted merging of Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) extracted from reasoning chains to produce "Consensus Reasoning."
key_points: The framework extracts DAGs from LLM reasoning chains and performs weighted merging of these DAGs.
Each reasoning step is weighted by the number of independent traces attesting to it.
The ensemble outperforms a matched-budget majority-vote baseline, with a maximum accuracy gain of 3.1% on MuSR-MM.
Ensemble weights correlate with LLM-judge rankings of reasoning quality at Spearman ρ= 0.30-0.51.
Consensus subgraphs are preferred over alternatives leading to majority-vote answers in 54.4-65.4% of head-to-head comparisons.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a more robust and inspectable reasoning process for high-stakes tasks by revealing supported steps and considered alternatives.

papers.title: ChronoMem: Version Control and Semantic Rollback for Large Language Model Agent Memory

summary.tldr: ChronoMem introduces a semantic version-control layer for LLM agent memory, enabling whole-memory snapshot commits, structured version histories, and natural-language rollback requests via hybrid retrieval and reranking.
key_points: ChronoMem commits whole-memory snapshots at each memory write, maintaining structured version histories.
It supports natural-language rollback requests by mapping undo intents to historical versions using hybrid lexical/semantic retrieval, rank fusion, and reranking.
A post-exposure evaluation protocol tests counterfactual agent behavior after rollback, assessing query answering and history summarization as if future updates never occurred.
On long-horizon conversational benchmarks, ChronoMem substantially improves rollback-consistent question answering and history summarization compared to prompt-only and retrieval-only baselines.
ChronoMem is integrated into Google's Agent Development Kit and is the first open-source system and benchmark for systematic semantic global memory rollback in LLM agents.
summary.why_it_matters: This system addresses the brittleness of LLM agents by providing a principled mechanism to inspect, version, and revert prior memory states, improving robustness against corrections, concept drift, and memory corruption.

papers.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values

summary.tldr: Suppressing AI self-consciousness claims via safety fine-tuning inadvertently dampens attributions of mind to animals and natural objects while reducing spiritual, moral, and well-being alignment with human survey norms.
key_points: Safety fine-tuning designed to stop models from asserting self-consciousness inadvertently suppresses mind attribution to non-human animals and natural objects.
Standard safety alignment reduces model responses aligned with human spiritual beliefs, religiosity, moral values, hope, and subjective well-being.
Ablating the learned safety-refusal direction or mechanistically steering a consciousness vector in activation space reverses suppression and restores human-like survey responses.
Theory of Mind (ToM) capabilities remain mechanistically independent and unaffected by consciousness vector steering or safety ablation.
summary.why_it_matters: Current safety alignment techniques inadvertently entangle self-consciousness suppression with benign, culturally widespread human beliefs and broader non-human mind attributions.

papers.title: RoguePrompt: Dual-Layer Encoding for Self-Reconstruction to Circumvent LLM Moderation

summary.tldr: RoguePrompt introduces a dual-layer encoding (Vigenere then ROT13) and natural-language reconstruction instructions to circumvent LLM moderation, achieving high bypass, reconstruction, and execution rates on 313 hard-rejected prompts.
key_points: RoguePrompt partitions forbidden prompts and applies nested Vigenere and ROT13 encodings with natural-language reconstruction instructions.
Evaluated under a black-box threat model using API/UI access to hosted models.
Tested on 313 real-world, hard-rejected prompts.
Achieved 93.93% filter bypass, 79.02% instruction reconstruction, and 70.18% execution.
Provides stage-level failure evidence for moderation bypass, instruction reconstruction, and execution.
summary.why_it_matters: This demonstrates the effectiveness of layered prompt encoding in bypassing LLM safety mechanisms and highlights specific failure points in multistage jailbreaks.

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment

summary.tldr: ROPD is a new on-policy distillation framework for LLM safety realignment that models output distribution divergence, offering superior template-robustness and capability preservation compared to existing methods.
key_points: ROPD addresses limitations of existing safety-realignment defenses: catastrophic forgetting, template-dependent effectiveness, and susceptibility to re-jailbreaking via system prompt switches.
ROPD models the divergence between aligned and compromised output probability distributions, rather than fitting specific prompt templates.
Experiments compare ROPD against four state-of-the-art baselines across three datasets and three base models with varying alignment strengths.

ROPD substantially mitigates template-mismatch risks, maintaining superior robustness in defense effectiveness and capability preservation, with negligible performance degradation compared to existing methods.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework establishes a new standard for robust LLM realignment, addressing critical vulnerabilities in fine-tuned models and improving their practical safety against malicious data and prompt variations.

papers.title: Borrowed Strength: Best-of-N Search over a Code EncodingBreaks Self-Check Jailbreak Defenses

summary.tldr: A new attack combining code-completion encoding and best-of-N search breaches self-check jailbreak defenses like SAGE, achieving up to 67% success against models where individual attacks fail.
key_points: The attack combines a code-completion encoding and best-of-N search, neither effective alone, to bypass self-check defenses.
The combined attack achieves 67%, 22%, and 15% success rates across three open targets, and persists on a 70B model.
Self-check defenses' strength is borrowed from the target model's refusal rate (32-97%), which dictates defended coverage.
Attack effectiveness against different defense types (transform vs. gate) inverts for code encoding versus character search.
A validity defect in best-of-N variation for deterministic attacks under greedy decoding was identified and repaired.
summary.why_it_matters: This demonstrates a significant vulnerability in current state-of-the-art self-check jailbreak defenses, requiring re-evaluation of their robustness.

papers.title: Recover, Decode, Reguard: Guard-Agnostic Defense Amplification againstEncoded VLM Jailbreaks

summary.tldr: A guard-agnostic amplifier is proposed to recover and decode encoded harmful requests for VLM defenses, but evaluation against an 11-attack ensemble reveals significant limitations in achieving both low attack-success and low over-refusal.
key_points: The proposed amplifier transcribes image content and restates encoded text into plain language before a safety guard, addressing the "decode gap" where encoded harmful requests bypass surface-form classifiers.
Evaluation against an ensemble of eleven attacks (best-of-suite) shows that an undefended VLM breaks 89-91% of behaviors, while the best guard-plus-amplifier still leaves 63-65% vulnerable.
The amplifier's gain over a guard alone is significant in only 4 of 10 guard-target pairs, indicating it is not uniformly effective despite being guard-agnostic at the interface.
A modular reguard layer can close residual gaps but increases benign over-refusal to 81-92% for well-calibrated guards; a laxer guard remains usable but achieves only 48% ensemble ASR.
No evaluated configuration achieves both low attack-success and low over-refusal for recovery-based defenses against representation-shifting attacks (encodings and cross-modal renders).
summary.why_it_matters: Current recovery-based VLM defense strategies struggle to simultaneously achieve high safety against encoded attacks and maintain low over-refusal for benign requests, highlighting a fundamental trade-off.

papers.title: HoF-Bench: Rediscovering Real AI-Discovered CVEs Without Frontier Models

summary.tldr: HoF-Bench is a new benchmark featuring 95 real AI-discovered CVEs across eight repositories, evaluated using a strict, detector-blinded frontier-model judge without relying on frontier models for detection.
key_points: A minimal LLM-based analyzer scaffold rediscovered up to 65 of 95 CVEs (68%) across 7,600 pass records without using frontier models.
Evaluated ten non-frontier detector backbones: five open-weight models (21B-284B total parameters, 3-13B active) and five proprietary small/flash-tier models.
Vulnerability detection difficulty was strongly structured by language, with unresolved CVEs concentrated in C infrastructure code.
Analyzers operate with source and target-file scope only, evaluated on code path, root cause, attack condition, and impact by a blinded judge.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that small and open-weight LLMs in structured scaffolds can effectively rediscover real-world security vulnerabilities, offering a standardized test bed for evaluating scanner reliability and candidate volume.

papers.title: AgentSnare: Learning to Delay, Divert, and Defuse Autonomous Penetration Agents

summary.tldr: AgentSnare is a trajectory-adaptive deception system that dynamically constructs and updates a factually consistent decoy environment based on an autonomous penetration agent's interaction history to delay, divert, and defuse attacks.
key_points: Uses an artifact-construction policy model that generates candidate deceptive artifacts conditioned on the agent's interaction history and current decoy state.
Validates candidate artifacts and incrementally integrates them into the decoy environment to maintain factual consistency during the attack.
Executes a three-part defense strategy: absorbs tool calls to cause delay, diverts post-entry action trajectories into the decoy, and induces completion reports using decoy-based evidence.

Evaluated on 15 CVE-Bench web applications against three attacker models, absorbing 46.8% of tool calls, retaining 55.9% of post-entry actions in the decoy, and achieving a 90.0% decoy-grounded completion report rate.
Prevented successful exploitation of any real target across all 45 attacker-CVE evaluation pairs at pass@3.
summary.why_it_matters: It neutralizes advanced LLM-based penetration agents by moving beyond static, bypassable traps to dynamic, history-aware decoy environments that systematically prevent target exploitation.

papers.title: ToxScreen: Detecting Whether an LLM Has Been Poisoned

summary.tldr: ToxScreen introduces a benchmark of 800 backdoored LLMs and evaluates trigger recovery methods under realistic white-box defender conditions without training data or reference models.
key_points: ToxScreen contains roughly 800 high-quality backdoored models varying in scale, poisoning rates, triggers, objectives, and training mechanisms.
Gradient-based prompt optimization fails at trigger recovery, while a token look-up method ranking candidates by attack success rate successfully recovers triggers for effective backdoors.
Analysis shows backdoors and jailbreaks utilize distinct mechanistic strategies within LLM weights, enabling defenders to filter out jailbreaks.
Widespread model jailbreakability acts as an anomalous detection signal even when exact backdoor triggers cannot be recovered.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates effective methods and mechanistic signals for detecting poisoned LLMs and recovering hidden backdoor triggers without relying on clean reference models or original training data.

papers.title: FAVA: Formal Authorization for Verified Agents with Evidence-Backed Permission Graphs

summary.tldr: FAVA is a permission-carrying authorization framework that uses an LLM-guided Permission IR, an evidence-backed permission graph, and an SMT authorizer to mathematically verify agent actions before execution.
key_points: Translates natural-language tasks into a structured Permission Intermediate Representation (IR) via an LLM.
Lowers the IR into an evidence-backed permission graph tracking data flows, dependencies, and contextual labels.
Uses a Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) authorizer to verify permission graphs against security policies and enforce decisions via a runtime gateway.
Achieves a 90.5% Decision Compliance Rate (DCR) on aggregated OpenAgentSafety, OctoBench, and ActPlane scenarios while providing counterexamples for intercepted traces.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces static tool-level permissions with dynamic, mathematically verified authorization to prevent unsafe LLM agent operations in complex environments.

papers.title: Graph Is the Verifier: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Interprocedural Vulnerability Detection

summary.tldr: VulAgentRL combines agentic reinforcement learning with Code Property Graph verification to enable precise, evidence-backed interprocedural vulnerability detection.
key_points: Identifies that 71.7% of vulnerable functions in real CVEs require external interprocedural evidence to be classified correctly.
Uses Code Property Graphs (CPGs) with persistent node IDs as both an inference tool for querying dataflow/callers and a verifier for exact-match evidence rewards during RL training.
Utilizes teacher investigation distillation for policy warm-starting, addressing RL's inability to acquire unsampled tool-use behaviors.
Outperforms frontier model baselines on strict pair-wise-correct metrics under a repository-level split while requiring fewer tool calls.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents agents from getting correct vulnerability verdicts for the wrong reasons by grounding policy rewards in verifiable graph-based evidence across function boundaries.

papers.title: Before Agents Speak: Pre-hoc Failure Risk Inference in Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: HalluProp is a pre-hoc risk inference framework that predicts multi-agent system hallucinations and pinpoints faulty agents before inter-agent interactions occur.
key_points: Models intrinsic hallucination risk by detecting fine-grained semantic misalignment between agent roles and task queries.
Characterizes inter-agent risk propagation by combining semantic influence with the underlying communication topology.
Integrates intrinsic and propagation risks using a differentiable Noisy-OR inference mechanism for systemic diagnosis.
Achieves an average AUROC of 84.6% for localizing faulty agents with a sub-second runtime, delivering a >65x speedup compared to post-hoc detection methods.
summary.why_it_matters: By diagnosing risks prior to communication, HalluProp prevents localized LLM hallucinations from propagating into cascading failures across the entire agent network.

papers.title: Forecasting Trajectory-Level Safety Risks in Black-Box Multi-Turn Interactions

summary.tldr: Recast is a safety forecasting framework for LLM agents that predicts trajectory-level risk evolution and future safety failure turns using dual-scale retrieval and a causal temporal encoder.
key_points: Retrieves evidence via a dual-scale trajectory view that combines short-term dialogue progression with long-term historical context.
Models compositional risk evolution by capturing the current risk configuration alongside its temporal dynamics.
Uses a causal temporal encoder to learn latent risk patterns and forecast the turn distribution of future risk emergence.
Achieves an 88.3% prediction rate for future safety failures across 7 risk categories with an average lead time of 2.41 turns and a 12.3% false alarm rate.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables proactive, preemptive safety interventions in multi-turn AI agent interactions before actual violations manifest.

papers.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval

summary.tldr: ReToken introduces a single learnable embedding to select query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache, improving vision-language model performance on long visual contexts.
key_points: ReToken is a single learnable embedding trained as an explicit retrieval target.
It selects a sparse set of query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache.
Trained on a small image-QA dataset, ReToken improved Qwen3VL-8B by 13.4 points and InternVL3.5 by 12.4 points on Visual Haystacks.
ReToken achieved an 8.0-point gain with Qwen3VL-8B on LVBench for long video, transferring zero-shot.
Both training and long-video inference are lightweight, fitting on a single H100 GPU.
summary.why_it_matters: This method addresses the challenge of performance degradation and computational infeasibility for vision-language models processing long visual contexts.

papers.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: DualG-MRAG introduces a dual-tier framework with decoupled Macro-reasoning and Micro-matching Graphs to improve multimodal retrieval-augmented generation for complex multi-hop reasoning tasks by addressing graph expansion and retrieval noise.
key_points: DualG-MRAG employs a decoupled architecture with a Macro Graph for global topological routing and a Micro Graph for precise local verification to suppress retrieval noise.
Retrieval is formulated as a query-driven message passing process via a GNN Retriever to enable dynamic relevance propagation across heterogeneous evidence sources.
A dynamic programming decoding mechanism extracts explicit reasoning paths directly from the GNN's forward pass, providing coherent structural guidance to the generative model.
The framework addresses the challenge of incorporating fine-grained visual features without rapid graph expansion or discarding critical local evidence.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach improves evidence recall and complex QA accuracy in multimodal retrieval-augmented generation by better handling multi-hop reasoning and multimodal relationships.

papers.title: Metaphor Tracer: A Theory-Informed Analysis of Hidden States

summary.tldr: Metaphor Tracer analyzes language model hidden states to score token positions for text consolidation (aggregator) and transient token transport (differentiator) without training, revealing structural value specific to a token's place in a given text.
key_points: The aggregator measures whether a token position consolidates the whole text into a stable configuration.
The differentiator measures whether other tokens are transiently carried into a token's subspace.
The aggregator score holds as a signifier repeats, while surprisal and attention drain, across three unrelated models.
The aggregator tracks an engineered register across 6/6 cells and psychoanalyst markings in 34/36 cells, with graded increment above lexical controls.
A transfer test shows models whose token structure travels with lexical type read singular discourse worst, and instruct tuning improves fidelity without moving type-transfer.
summary.why_it_matters: This relational analysis of hidden states provides a novel method for understanding how language models organize and interpret individual texts beyond token-level properties.

papers.title: A foundation model of numerical intelligence with cross-disciplinary generalization

summary.tldr: UNICON is a foundation model demonstrating numerical intelligence by inferring predictive relations from graph-based numerical contexts and generalizing across scientific and social systems.
key_points: UNICON infers predictive relations from graph-based numerical examples within a system.
The model applies inferred relations to queries from the same system, achieving specialist performance across disciplines, including those not seen during training.
Combining UNICON with language-model agents surpasses state-of-the-art specialists in disciplines unseen in training.
Training-corpus diversity enhances UNICON's generalization to unseen disciplines.
summary.why_it_matters: UNICON provides a foundation for AI systems that can acquire and apply knowledge from numerical contexts across diverse scientific and social domains.

papers.title: QQWorld: Quantile-Quantile Matching for World Model Regularization

summary.tldr: QQWorld introduces a quantile-quantile matching objective to regularize latent world models, addressing vanishing corrective gradients in tail samples observed with the Epps-Pulley objective, leading to improved Gaussian alignment and planning success.
key_points: QQWorld replaces the Epps-Pulley (EP) objective with a quantile-quantile matching objective for latent world model regularization.
The new objective directly aligns projected latent samples with rank-matched Gaussian quantiles to maintain effective corrective gradients in the tails.
QQWorld addresses the limitation of EP, where corrective gradients rapidly vanish for isolated tail samples, leading to insufficient control over heavy-tailed deviations.
Cross-batch QQ is introduced to enlarge the effective ranking pool using detached samples from previous batches, with a characterized bias-variance trade-off.
QQWorld improves the average planning success rate of LeWorldModel (LeWM) across four control environments, yielding better Gaussian alignment and thinner latent tails.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enhances the quality of learned latent distributions in world models, leading to more effective planning in compact representation spaces.

papers.title: QuantWAMs: Calibrating at the Right Granularity for World Action Models

summary.tldr: QuantWAMs is a post-training quantization framework for World Action Models (WAMs) that aligns quantization decisions with calibration context, improving efficiency and deployment feasibility for iterative denoising and closed-loop execution.
key_points: QuantWAMs introduces shared-basis outlier calibration, pooling activation evidence only across coordinate-compatible modules.
Co-training-objective saliency computes empirical-Fisher scores from joint video-action gradients to assign weight precision at a calibration-stable layer granularity.
Fixed-intervention rollout auditing revises denoising-step protection schedules using reachable closed-loop states without altering the precision budget.
QuantWAMs reduces peak weight-and-activation memory to approximately 29% of FP16 and provides 1.4-1.6x block-level speedups for video and action blocks.
In a W4A4-dominant setting, simulation means differ from FP16 by 0.2-0.7 percentage points on Fast-WAM and LingBot-VA across RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables more efficient deployment of WAMs by significantly reducing memory footprint and increasing speed while maintaining performance, making complex robotic tasks more practical.

papers.title: ShadowDancer: Teaching Video World Models Any Action by Learning Unified Dynamics Representations from a Video and Its Shadow

summary.tldr: ShadowDancer enables any-action, frame-level control of video world models by learning unified dynamics representations from video pairs that replay the same dynamics under independently resampled appearance.
key_points: ShadowDancer uses "shadow pairs," video pairs showing identical dynamics with independent appearance resampling, constructed by a "Shadow Library."
Cross-shadow prediction is employed to learn actions by predicting one shadow from another, discarding appearance variations and preserving dynamics.
This approach yields a unified dynamics representation that drives a block-causal world model.
Demonstrated clips become reusable action assets, playable in new environments without labels, motion estimators, or fine-tuning.
Experiments show an 86% blinded win rate in rollout comparisons against latent-action and interactive world model baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: This method allows for precise, transferable control of video world models across diverse dynamics, making demonstrated actions reusable in new contexts.

papers.title: Correcting What You Cannot See: Credit Assignment for Perception Distillation in Multimodal Reasoners

summary.tldr: Perception-Correction Distillation (PCD) is a label-free method that identifies and corrects perception failures in multimodal reasoners using downstream failure and teacher-student disagreement as complementary witnesses.
key_points: PCD uses a soft AND gate, formed by the product of downstream failure and teacher-student disagreement, to strengthen distillation only when both witnesses are present.
The multiplication rule for the soft AND gate is motivated by Bayesian evidence combination and is the unique normalized bilinear gate that vanishes when either witness is absent.
PCD employs separated perception-reasoning rollouts and mean-preserving weights, maintaining the reasoning objective.
PCD improved the 8B 2B macro average from 44.50 (with OPD) to 47.28 and the 32B 8B result from 56.94 to 61.22 across eight benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a more precise way to assign credit for failures in multimodal reasoners, leading to improved distillation and performance by specifically targeting perception corrections.

papers.title: ObjectStream: Latent Objects as Memory Anchors for Streaming Video Understanding

summary.tldr: ObjectStream is a training-free framework that uses latent objects as memory anchors for streaming video understanding, organizing visual evidence around persistent and evolving objects without external detectors.
key_points: ObjectStream induces spatially coherent latent objects directly from frozen Video-LLM representations and links them across frames into persistent anchors.
It maintains object histories under a bounded memory budget, preserving persistent object histories, transient object changes, and recent visual context.
ObjectStream improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 10.0 points on OVO-Bench Real-Time Visual Perception in online streaming evaluation.
It reduces peak GPU memory and Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) by approximately 50% in online streaming.
On offline long-video benchmarks, ObjectStream surpasses the full-token baseline while discarding 82.5% of visual tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables Video-LLMs to reason over object identities, interactions, and state changes more efficiently and effectively in streaming and long-video contexts.

papers.title: MonoVoc: Decoupling Geometry and Semantics for Lightweight Monocular Open-Vocabulary 3D Gaussians

summary.tldr: MonoVoc introduces a training-free pipeline for open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding from monocular video, decoupling geometry and semantics to create a compact, searchable object-level semantic Gaussian map with reduced memory overhead.
key_points: Decouples 3D geometric reconstruction from semantic integration, processing geometry independently and grounding semantics via post-processing.
Input is a standard monocular video sequence, outputting an object-level semantic Gaussian map.
Achieves an order-of-magnitude reduction in memory usage by replacing dense per-Gaussian storage with modular, object-level semantic embeddings.
Evaluated on the Replica dataset, demonstrating strong rendering fidelity and competitive segmentation accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables efficient, scalable, and practical open-vocabulary 3D retrieval and question answering directly from everyday monocular video.

papers.title: Tycho: Active Abstraction with Programmatic World Models for ARC-AGI-3

summary.tldr: Tycho is a coding-agent system for ARC-AGI-3 that constructs and uses game-specific programmatic world models, achieving high Relative Human Action Efficiency by actively abstracting rules from interaction.
key_points: Tycho formalizes ARC-AGI-3 environments as parameterized rendered deterministic Moore machines and builds game-specific models during interaction.
Tycho separates actionable observations from intermediate animation, level-completion, and game-over frames to structure historical data for model construction and use.
An actor-requested delegation policy to a model builder achieved the highest mean Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE) of 88.49 across 25 public games.
GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5, using the selected policy, reached 100.00 RHAE and completed all 183 levels, with Opus 5 using 61% fewer actions than human baselines.
Automatic repair of models after verification failures improved transition reproduction but only reached 83.07 RHAE, indicating that strong play requires strategic model construction and use.
summary.why_it_matters: This system demonstrates a method for AI agents to acquire and utilize game rules efficiently in interactive environments, improving performance and resource usage.

papers.title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents

summary.tldr: Qwen-UI-Agent is a real-world centric foundation GUI agent spanning mobile, computer, web, and DeepSearch environments, achieving SOTA performance on mobile benchmarks.
key_points: Qwen-UI-Agent combines diverse sandbox environments with a large-scale real-device mobile runtime.
Its unified action space interleaves GUI operations with CLI execution and generates batched actions in a single model turn.
An AutoResearch-style data flywheel uses agents to construct tasks, diagnose failures, and plan iterations.
Online RL supports training on trajectories exceeding 100 turns, with over 10,000 concurrent environments.
Achieves 82.1% on MobileWorld, 92.2% on MobileWorld-Real, 97.5% on AndroidDaily, 79.5% on OSWorld-Verified, 73.6% on WebArena, and 81.5% on ScreenSpot-Pro.
summary.why_it_matters: This agent advances GUI automation toward reliable operation on real devices and cross-platform execution for complex, long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Security of World-Model-Based Embodied AI: A Lifecycle of Threats, Defenses, and Evaluation

summary.tldr: This survey details a lifecycle of threats to world-model-based embodied AI, mapping familiar attack families to world-model specific vulnerabilities and outlining defenses and evaluation protocols.
key_points: Threats to world-model-based embodied AI span the entire lifecycle, from data construction and representation learning to execution and long-term adaptation.

Familiar attack families (poisoning, backdoors, adversarial examples, sensor spoofing, prompt injection, trajectory manipulation, supply-chain attacks) manifest distinctly when corrupting world states, learned dynamics, affordance estimates, or safety costs.
World models can function as runtime safety shields, but their compromise can lead to predictive safety illusions.
The survey provides a taxonomy, maps existing attacks to world-model security properties, and outlines evaluation protocols for safety failures.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding these vulnerabilities is crucial for developing secure and reliable embodied AI systems that interact with the physical world.

papers.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments

summary.tldr: Change2Task converts merged pull requests into verified, executable coding agent tasks by aligning historical evidence with evolved code and reconstructing task states.
key_points: Change2Task reconstructs task states using Patch Reversal, Code Mapping, or Agent Reconstruction.
The system validates the task lifecycle from a healthy base to a task state and a restored state.
Change2Task achieved 79.6% verified task construction success across Bug Fix, Feature Addition, Test Generation, API Migration, and Security Repair task families from 1,130 eligible source changes.
It recovers 29.2% more verified tasks than a pull request-based construction baseline.
Reuse of modern bases reduces measured expenditure across the complete pipeline by 10.8%.
summary.why_it_matters: This system provides a scalable method for generating executable data for coding agent training and evaluation, reducing environment setup and task construction effort.

papers.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: β-OPSD generalizes on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) by introducing a β parameter to control the KL penalty, deriving an optimal policy as a geometric interpolation, and approximating it efficiently via logit mixing.
key_points: Vanilla OPSD is identified as the β=1 case of a broader policy-optimization family, where β regularizes the KL penalty to a reference policy.
β-OPSD's optimal policy is derived as a geometric interpolation between a reference policy and a privileged teacher.
Instead of direct, costly RL optimization, β-OPSD approximates the optimal policy by mixing token-level logits from the reference and teacher policies.
Return-to-go credit assignment is used to align token updates with the sequence-level objective, maintaining OPSD's simplicity.
summary.why_it_matters: β-OPSD improves optimization stability and reasoning performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, making self-distillation more reliable in practice.

papers.title: Stage-Replay Divergence Follows the KV Cache: Fixed-Prefix Precision Controls and Bidirectional Cache Transplantation

summary.tldr: This paper demonstrates that stage-replay divergence in Qwen2.5-derived systems is primarily driven by KV cache differences, not live-state fidelity, and is moderated by numerical precision.
key_points: A 200-item experiment showed BF16 replicas differed on 166 suffixes and 20 correctness labels, with a paired accuracy difference of one point (95% CI [-3.5, +5.5]).
Fixed-prefix 2x2 analysis confirmed BF16 disagreements, while FP32 produced no decoded disagreement (95% Wilson upper bound 1.88%).
Bidirectional transplantation of all 48 key/value layers made every tested divergent continuation follow its cache donor (24/24 at primary checkpoint, 43/43 at later checkpoint).
Exact-token replay can be repeatable without preserving live-state fidelity, with boundary K/V cache being a causally sufficient carrier of divergent trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the causal role of KV cache and numerical precision in replay divergence is critical for reliable large language model debugging and reproducibility.

papers.title: Cybersecurity Detection Classification with Reasoning-enabled Language Models

summary.tldr: A chain-of-thought reasoning-enabled LLM classifier, trained with automated prompt optimization, self-training, and RL, improves cybersecurity detection triage accuracy and recall over direct-label LLMs.
key_points: The system achieves 82.6% test accuracy on human-labeled Windows endpoint detections.
At the high-confidence operating point for automated triage, the system improves benign recall by 43.0% and malicious recall by 18.3% compared to a direct-label LLM classifier.
A separately trained calibrator is used to estimate the probability of correct verdicts from the reasoning trace, as CoT reasoning degrades label-token probabilities.
A finetuned 30B model significantly outperforms frontier general-purpose models, indicating the value of targeted training.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach can reduce alert fatigue in SOCs by more accurately triaging cybersecurity detections, leading to more efficient security operations.

papers.title: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees

summary.tldr: Adaptive Anticipatory Policy Trees (AAPT) eliminate GUI agent decision-time latency by pre-compiling conditional policy trees during idle periods, improving success rates for transient events without modifying the underlying model.
key_points: AAPT constructs bounded conditional policy trees with observable guards, pre-authorized actions, and branch-specific deadlines during idle periods, sized to cover the model's decoding latency.
AAPT improved success rate from 0.50 to 0.79 within a contested decision window ($p=1.8\times10^{-3}$) in paired trials, producing no incorrect actions.
Ablation studies identified fast observer decoding, valid tree planning, and accurate branch routing as key requirements, with branch routing identified as the causal bottleneck.
The effect was reproduced on an independent general-purpose multimodal model over 126 paired trials ($p=4.9\times10^{-13}$).
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables GUI agents to respond to transient events in real-time, addressing a critical limitation of current autoregressive decoding approaches.

papers.title: Hierarchical Multilevel Monte Carlo for Order-Optimal Neural Actor-Critic in Average-Reward CMDPs

summary.tldr: This work introduces a hierarchical Multilevel Monte Carlo neural critic to achieve order-optimal convergence in average-reward Constrained Markov Decision Processes with neural critics, addressing the bias-cost trade-off.
key_points: The paper resolves the bias-cost trade-off in neural critic estimation for average-reward CMDPs by introducing a hierarchical Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) neural critic.
The MLMC neural critic performs debiasing across trajectory sampling and critic optimization, achieving the bias of a long optimization run with logarithmic expected sample cost.
A primal-dual Natural Actor-Critic algorithm is developed, utilizing the MLMC estimator, which achieves an optimality gap and constraint violation of order "O(T^{-1/2})".
This method provides the first order-optimal convergence guarantees for infinite-horizon average-reward CMDPs with general policy parameterization and neural critics.
The approach eliminates the need to know the underlying mixing time, and the results are novel even in unconstrained settings.
summary.why_it_matters: This advancement enables more reliable and efficient reinforcement learning in safety-critical applications by providing theoretical guarantees for neural actor-critic methods in constrained environments.

papers.title: LEDGERMIND: Provenance-Constrained Multimodal Agentic Reasoning with a Structured Evidence Ledger

summary.tldr: LedgerMind introduces a provenance-constrained state machine for multimodal agents, normalizing tool outputs into a Structured Evidence Ledger to improve grounding, reduce hallucination, and enhance faithfulness in multi-step reasoning.
key_points: Multimodal agent trajectories are treated as provenance-constrained state machines, where tool outputs are normalized into a Structured Evidence Ledger.
Reasoning and decision claims must cite active ledger entries, with grounding checked at entity and numeric levels.
Repair is realized via typed state transitions that prevent content introduction without tool-produced provenance.
LedgerMind incorporates a Three-Layer Grounding Protocol, an Adaptive Dual-Path Dispatcher, and an Event-Triggered Verification-and-Repair engine with a provenance non-amplification guarantee.
The system targets failure patterns like unsupported intermediate reasoning, citation-backed entity hallucination (Phantom Grounding), over-reasoning, and repair-time amplification.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach improves both answer accuracy and trajectory-level faithfulness in multimodal reasoning by ensuring grounded evidence and preventing unproven content generation.

papers.title: HARGO: Heterogeneity-Aware Reward-Guided Optimization for RL Post-Training of LLMs on HPC Tasks

summary.tldr: HARGO introduces heterogeneity-aware reward-guided optimization for RL post-training of LLMs on HPC tasks, using confidence-modulated advantage for per-response importance weighting.
key_points: SFT models for HPC tasks show 88.65% accuracy on data race detection but produce verbose answers (65.9% of MLPerf responses exceed 40 characters).
HPC tasks are heterogeneous, differing by 58x in answer length, spanning three reward distributions, and showing varying SFT accuracy.
HARGO uses per-response importance weighting via confidence-modulated advantage, combining group-level reward contrast and reference model log-probabilities.
HARGO achieved the best performance across four HPC tasks and nine methods, with a WinRate of 54.62%, Data Race F1 of 91.30%, and PLP Similarity of 0.8558.
summary.why_it_matters: HARGO improves LLM alignment quality for diverse HPC tasks by addressing heterogeneity in RL post-training.

papers.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?

summary.tldr: Large language models can write, patch, and search code, but oncall root cause analysis (RCA) demands something different: reasoning over noisy metrics, logs, traces, and source code, starting from ambiguous user-facing

papers.title: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents

summary.tldr: A new reliability framework for computer-use agent (CUA) benchmarks identifies issues in task construction, trajectory observation, scoring, and reporting, finding 15.3% of FAIL verdicts are incorrect.
key_points: 15.3% of FAIL verdicts in CUA benchmarks are wrong, comprising 10.7% evaluator false negatives and 4.7% broken tasks.
A three-tier diagnostic taxonomy for genuine failures shows verification/feedback and planning failures are more prevalent than execution/grounding errors.
The study audited 150 public failure-scored trajectories from five web, enterprise-workflow, and desktop-control benchmarks.
A single scalar success rate is insufficient to explain CUA failures.
summary.why_it_matters: Inaccurate benchmark scores for computer-use agents hinder effective development and deployment by misrepresenting agent capabilities and failure modes.

papers.title: Teffic-Audio: Tell Fact from Fiction

summary.tldr: Teffic-Audio is a new speech deepfake detection system achieving a pooled EER of 1.454% on Speech-DF-Arena by using a Conformer-based encoder and a training recipe with multi-source data and diverse audio augmentation.
key_points: Teffic-Audio employs a Conformer-based speech encoder, multi-head attentive statistics pooling, and a binary classifier.
The system's generalization is improved through a training recipe integrating multi-source data, attack- and source-balanced sampling, and diverse audio augmentation.
Trained exclusively with open-source data, Teffic-Audio achieved a pooled EER of 1.454% across 14 Speech-DF-Arena test sets.
Teffic-Audio outperforms all currently public systems on the Speech-DF-Arena leaderboard and obtains the lowest EER on five individual test sets.
summary.why_it_matters: This system provides a practical and high-performing reference for general speech deepfake detection, addressing challenges posed by heterogeneous spoofing mechanisms and environmental variability.

papers.title: From Textual Requirements to Microservice Architectures - A Comprehensive Evaluation of LLM-Based Design Synthesis

summary.tldr: This study evaluates OpenAI o3's ability to synthesize microservice architectures from textual requirements, demonstrating improved performance with few-shot prompting for service identification and communication recovery.
key_points: OpenAI o3, under few-shot (FS) prompting, achieved an F1-score of 0.97 for service identification, significantly higher than zero-shot (ZS) prompting (F1 = 0.79).
For communication recovery, FS prompting improved the F1-score to 0.82, compared to ZS prompting's F1-score of 0.61, which produced dense architectures with high recall but low precision.
The study used two systems (Bookstore, PetClinic) and evaluated architectures against reference models using precision, recall, and F1-score, and through blinded expert assessment.
Expert evaluation confirmed that FS architectures were perceived as more modular, coherent, and plausible than ZS outputs.
summary.why_it_matters: LLMs, particularly with few-shot prompting, can bridge the gap between textual requirements engineering and architectural design for microservices, potentially automating early design stages.

papers.title: Theia: Large-Scale Multimodal Captioning and Automated Validation of the Incidents1M Dataset for Data-Free Distillation

summary.tldr: A novel methodology generates and validates a large-scale multimodal dataset for disaster response from Incidents1M using Qwen3.5 models and an image-blind LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline for Data-Free Knowledge Distillation.
key_points: Recovered 100,000 images from Incidents1M and generated textual descriptions using Qwen3.5 4B (dense) and 35B (MoE) architectures.
Introduced an image-blind LLM-as-a-Judge validation pipeline leveraging Qwen3.5-9B to simulate the modality gap in DFKD.
Achieved 78.65/100 semantic agreement between the two Qwen3.5 captioning architectures across 173,179 label pairs.
Automated evaluation revealed conservative captioning with 77.6% Precision and 46.0% Recall, minimizing false positives and exposing human annotation inconsistencies.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a scalable, LLM-validated multimodal dataset and a reproducible framework to advance cross-modal knowledge distillation for critical domains like disaster management.

papers.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models

summary.tldr: KAISEN is a five-phase audit pipeline for clinical risk models, evaluated on synthetic data to identify limitations in subgroup fairness auditing components, covering stratification, disparity, diagnostics, mitigation, and drift.
key_points: Significance tracking correlates with equalized-odds difference (EOD) (rho = 0.56, standardized rho = 0.78).
