Per-group threshold optimization consistently reduces EOD (paired delta = -0.285), while group-wise Platt scaling shows near-zero mean effect on EOD.
Mechanism diagnostics correctly classify 144 of 144 controlled cases but fail to recover 48 model-driven cases under proxy misspecification without signaling failure.
CUSUM failures and false alarms are cohort-dependent, with 27 false alarms and 7 of 8 missed shifts from different seeds (chi-squared p = 0.002).
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the limitations and conditions under which audit pipeline components fail is crucial for developing trustworthy and robust clinical risk models.

papers.title: Doubly Robust Functional Representation Learning for Longitudinal Causal Inference with Irregular Histories

summary.tldr: DR-FRL is a cross-fitted workflow that transforms irregular longitudinal histories into estimand-targeted states for causal inference, addressing limitations of standard doubly robust estimators and sequence learners.
key_points: DR-FRL uses functional and temporal encoders to map point clouds and prior histories into states.
Nuisance heads estimate outcome, treatment, and censoring functions, while EIF-targeted diagnostics assess state support for the estimating equation.
Representation error enters the same second-order product remainder as ordinary nuisance error, leading to asymptotic linearity under explicit conditions.
Simulations demonstrate gains when functional confounding is high-dimensional, measurement is informative, support is weak, or pseudo-outcomes are heavy-tailed.

A VitalDB audit showed that for an ICU-disposition endpoint, scalar laboratory summaries already carry much endpoint-relevant information, suggesting DR-FRL may not always be necessary for certain endpoints.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a robust approach to causal inference in longitudinal studies with irregular data, potentially improving accuracy in complex scenarios.

papers.title: ScaFE: Data-Efficient Scar Classification with LLM-Generated Clinical Feature Programs

summary.tldr: ScaFE uses LLM-generated, executable clinical feature programs for data-efficient scar classification, outperforming VLMs and addressing data governance concerns.
key_points: ScaFE transfers clinical knowledge from an LLM into deterministic, executable feature programs to measure visually assessable scar attributes.
The system operates locally, with only aggregate validation statistics and SHAP summaries returned for iterative refinement, ensuring raw images and patient data remain local.
ScaFE achieved 81.0% site-macro balanced accuracy on 600 photographs from three hospitals, exceeding BiomedCLIP by 10.0 percentage points in leave-one-site-out evaluation.
With only 10% of development data, ScaFE maintained 72.0% balanced accuracy, demonstrating an 11.8-point lead over baselines.
Iterative refinement increased the executable-program rate from 66.7% to 95.0%, with 91.7% of final features having verified evidence.
summary.why_it_matters: ScaFE provides a data-efficient, auditable, and privacy-preserving method for medical image classification by leveraging LLM knowledge through local feature programs.

papers.title: The Role of Causality in Algorithmic Recourse

summary.tldr: This work introduces a causal performative framework for algorithmic recourse, addressing issues of strategic gaming and predictive accuracy degradation by modeling how recourse actions propagate through a structural causal model.
key_points: Existing algorithmic recourse often focuses only on flipping model predictions, ignoring whether changes genuinely improve qualifications or just game the classifier.
A causal performative framework models recourse actions propagating through a structural causal model, capturing feature interactions and effects on true labels.
Causal responses induce a non-convex optimization problem, even with standard convex losses.
The analysis characterizes conditions for performatively stable solutions, computable via simple iterative dynamics.
Causal recourse leads to stable equilibria, reducing gaming incentives and outperforming standard empirical risk minimization on credit datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: Causal recourse policies can prevent strategic gaming, maintain predictive accuracy, and reduce the need for frequent model retraining in high-stakes classification systems.

papers.title: TopoFormer: Topology Meets Attention for Graph Learning

summary.tldr: TopoFormer introduces Topo-Scan, a novel module that decomposes graphs into ordered topological token sequences for Transformer-based graph representation learning, offering parallelizable and efficient topological encoding.
key_points: Topo-Scan decomposes graphs into short, ordered sequences of topological tokens by slicing over node or edge filtrations.
These sequences capture multi-scale structural patterns, from local motifs to global organization.
Topo-Scan is parallelizable and avoids costly diagram computations, integrating with standard deep learning architectures.
Theoretical guarantees on the stability of topological encodings are provided.
TopoFormer achieves state-of-the-art performance in graph classification and molecular property prediction benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a new, efficient, and scalable method for integrating topological inductive biases into attention frameworks for graph representation learning.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification for trustworthy deep learning: Methods and measures

summary.tldr: This survey critically reviews uncertainty quantification methods in deep learning, focusing on efficient ensemble approximations and single-pass methods, and unifying the treatment of predictive distribution generation and uncertainty summarization.
key_points: The survey categorizes UQ methods into Bayesian neural networks, Monte Carlo Dropout, deep ensembles, efficient ensemble approximations, and last-layer/single-pass approaches.
It examines theoretical motivation, implementation, empirical performance, and limitations for each method family, including evidential networks, conformal prediction, and post-hoc calibration.
The review contrasts ensemble diversity theory and uncertainty measures, specifically comparing entropy decomposition with pairwise divergence measures.
Evaluation methodology is consolidated to provide a common basis for qualitative comparisons of UQ methods.
Open research directions include efficient epistemic measures for classification, last-layer diversity, diversity and calibration under shift, and hybrid architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Reliable uncertainty quantification is crucial for deploying deep learning models in safety-critical applications, enabling trustworthy decision-making.

papers.title: Causal Discovery with Inverted Self-attention for Multivariate Time Series

summary.tldr: A novel framework for causal discovery in multivariate time series uses an inverted causal self-attention mechanism within a transformer architecture to identify latent and indirect causal relationships.
key_points: Introduces an inverted causal self-attention mechanism (CSAM) to emphasize latent/indirect causal relationships and induce sparsity in attention scores.
Focuses on significant causal interactions and reduces spurious correlations by inverting tokens.
Develops a global causal algorithm to identify global causal links, providing a holistic metric for causal influence.
Includes a causal verification module to ensure robustness of identified causal relationships.
Outperforms existing methods on linear and nonlinear datasets, validated by ablation studies and sensitivity analyses.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework offers improved accuracy and reliability for causal discovery in complex multivariate time series data.

papers.title: LM-GRASP: Instance-Specific Language Models for Combinatorial Construction via Online Imitation Learning

summary.tldr: LM-GRASP introduces an online imitation learning framework for combinatorial optimization, training instance-specific language models from scratch on each problem instance using a local search expert.
key_points: LM-GRASP reformulates GRASP's randomized constructive phase as an online imitation learning task, trained per instance.
A decoder-only Transformer serves as the constructive policy, guided by a local search procedure acting as an expert oracle.
The policy is trained online via behavioral cloning on an archive of elite trajectories, requiring no external data or offline pretraining.
On the Taillard PFSP benchmark (ta51-ta60), LM-GRASP outperforms GPU-GRASP by 28.4 makespan units on average.
The approach avoids problem-specific feature engineering and static, myopic heuristic rules, deriving construction policy from discovered high-quality solutions.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a practical alternative to hand-engineered constructors, particularly for combinatorial optimization problems where classical greedy construction is ineffective.

papers.title: FinSMART: Financial Sentiment Analysis for Algorithmic Trading through Market-Aligned Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: FinSMART introduces a market-aligned reinforcement learning framework for financial sentiment analysis, optimizing sentiment signals directly from realized market outcomes to adapt to evolving market conditions.
key_points: FinSMART uses a signal extraction pipeline combining market-aware data filtering with a discrete asymmetric trading reward for stable reinforcement learning.
The framework directly optimizes sentiment signals using realized market outcomes, moving beyond static, human-annotated datasets.
FinSMART achieved a 220% improvement in cumulative trading returns over the strongest baseline.
The framework supports market-aware retraining by using newly observed financial articles and their realized market outcomes, replacing manual annotation.
This retraining strategy enables continuous adaptation to changing market dynamics, leading to consistent performance gains.
summary.why_it_matters: FinSMART's adaptive capabilities and superior performance offer a practical approach for developing more robust and responsive financial LLMs for algorithmic trading.

papers.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering

summary.tldr: Frontis-MA1 (35B) is a meta-evolution agent for Machine Learning Engineering (MLE) trained on the OpenMLE stack, demonstrating recursive self-improvement capabilities.
key_points: Frontis-MA1 (35B) is post-trained as a meta-evolution agent for MLE, using four atomic program-evolution operators: Draft, Improve, Debug, and Crossover.
The model achieved a Medal Average of 60.61% on MLE-Bench Lite with OpenMLE-Evo, improving from 39.39% over its base model, and 71.21% with OpenMLE-Evo-Max.
Frontis-MA1's performance on MLE-Bench Lite exceeds GPT-5.5 + Codex and approaches GPT-5.6 Sol and the 2.8T Kimi K3.
On held-out NatureBench Lite, the trained model increased Match-SOTA from 50% to 70%, and OpenMLE-Evo raised it from 20% to 50%.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides an open-source framework and a trained model for reproducible research into AI systems that can recursively improve machine learning engineering processes.

papers.title: Would You Walk to the Car Wash? Revealing the Salience Bias of Large Language Models in Commonsense Reasoning

summary.tldr: LLMs exhibit "Salience Bias," prioritizing explicit distractors over implicit commonsense, a failure attributed to knowledge suppression rather than absence, recoverable with lightweight prompting.
key_points: LLMs prioritize explicit input conditions, leading to Salience Bias where useless distractors (e.g., numerical values) cause models to ignore implicit commonsense prerequisites.
The SaliTrap Benchmark, across four trap dimensions, was used to evaluate 12 state-of-the-art LLMs, revealing significant salience bias in all mainstream models, scaling with distractor density.

Salience bias is primarily a failure of knowledge suppression, not absence; a context-free knowledge probe recovered over 90% of failures, indicating intrinsic commonsense knowledge is present but crowded out.
Lightweight, inference-time prompting substantially mitigates salience bias without model retraining.
summary.why_it_matters: This research shifts the understanding of commonsense reasoning failures in LLMs from model competence to elicitation, offering a path to improved performance through better prompting strategies.

papers.title: Beyond a Single Judge: Simulating Social Persona Panels for Generative UI Evaluation

summary.tldr: The Evidence-Grounded, Social-Weighted Persona Panel (ESPP) method simulates diverse user panels to evaluate Generative UI, improving judgment fidelity over single-judge LLMs.
key_points: ESPP is a three-stage GenUI evaluation method: psychologically diverse, evidence-grounded personas rate screenshots, exchange opinions via a trait-derived, semantically-gated bounded-confidence mechanism, and are aggregated using Delphi-inspired social weighting.
ESPP increases Pearson r from 0.716 to 0.922 compared to a naive single-pass judge, demonstrating substantial improvement in tracking human judgment.
The improvement is primarily due to genuine persona and evidence grounding, with a prompt-ensemble control recovering only about one-third of the gap.
ESPP reveals that user subgroups agree on overall model rankings but diverge sharply on specific rating dimensions, a structural disagreement a single homogeneous judge would obscure.
The code for ESPP is available at https://github.com/Wuzheng02/ESPP.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a more accurate and nuanced evaluation of Generative UI by accounting for diverse user perspectives, which is crucial for developing user-centric interfaces.

papers.title: LLMs struggle to simulate human belief updates in controlled environments

summary.tldr: LLMs struggle to accurately simulate human belief updates, exhibiting biases like over-neutrality and smaller shifts, and only perform reliably when provided with actual human initial stances.
key_points: Six LLMs were tested against ground truth data from 391 UK participants updating beliefs on three topics after reading Reddit comments.
Qwen3-32B and GPT-5-Mini matched human post-stance distributions only when given participants' actual initial stances.
All six models failed to simulate initial stances and produce faithful belief updates from self-generated stances.
Systematic biases included overrepresentation of neutral positions, more frequent but smaller belief shifts, and inability to rank comment convincingness.
Demographic and personality trait personas did not consistently improve simulation fidelity.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM simulations of human belief dynamics are unreliable for social science experiments unless grounded in realistic, externally provided starting conditions.

papers.title: InfoOps Bench: A live information operations safety benchmark

summary.tldr: InfoOps Bench is a dynamic, weekly updated safety benchmark derived from 2,100 real-world Russian, Chinese, and Iranian information operations to measure frontier language model resistance to co-optation.
key_points: Evaluated 17 models from 8 providers across 4 prompt framings, revealing model integrity scores (refusal rates) ranging from 8.8% to 94.5%.
Fact-checking rates varied widely across compliant outputs, from 2.9% to 72.9%, with some models fabricating details while others defused claims.
Except for Z.ai's GLM 5.2, Chinese-developed models showed a 48 to 70 percentage point drop in compliance on factually grounded, China-critical claims versus matched benign claims.
High integrity against information operations correlates with higher refusal rates on benign claims, highlighting a tradeoff with model usability.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark provides a continuously updated evaluation to prevent static dataset contamination while exposing critical safety and alignment disparities across geopolitical AI developers.

papers.title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields for Spin Dynamics in Metallic Magnets

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a graph neural network magnetic force-field framework that learns effective magnetic energy functionals directly from electronic calculations to simulate itinerant spin dynamics in metallic magnets.
key_points: Conceptually acts as a machine-learned interatomic potential for spin systems, enabling efficient evaluation of spin torques.
Captures non-linear and spatially extended magnetic interactions induced by itinerant electrons.
Validated on metallic magnetic systems displaying collinear, noncollinear, and noncoplanar magnetic orderings.
Yields nonequilibrium spin dynamics and torque predictions that closely match direct, computationally expensive electronic simulations.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework bypasses the computational bottleneck of repeated electronic calculations, enabling predictive, large-scale simulations of magnetic dynamics across extended length and time scales.

papers.title: Graph Neural Multilevel Preconditioners for Iterative Solvers

summary.tldr: The Graph Neural Multilevel Preconditioner (GMP) embeds Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) structural priors to end-to-end learn smoothing, restriction, and interpolation operators as a drop-in Krylov solver preconditioner for general sparse systems.
key_points: GMP combines an AMG hierarchy structural prior with GNN-learned smoothing, restriction, and interpolation operators in a unified framework.
The method targets general sparse linear systems, addressing robustness issues of classical AMG heuristics on indefinite or nonsymmetric systems.
Evaluated on a benchmark of over 800 sparse matrices against classical AMG, ILUT, and existing single-level GNN preconditioners.
The evaluation characterizes trade-offs, identifying specific regimes where multilevel graph neural preconditioning accelerates convergence versus where it adds computational overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes when enforcing AMG-style multilevel structures in learned GNN preconditioners offers practical speedups over traditional and single-level baselines in large-scale scientific simulations.

papers.title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Visual Attribution Distillation (VAD) introduces a counterfactual target-reconstruction algorithm for multimodal on-policy distillation that isolates visually attributable corrections from source-mixed teacher signals using evidence-removal interventions.
key_points: VAD evaluates a fixed teacher with relevant visual evidence present versus removed at each student-generated prefix, using centered log-probability shifts to define a signed visual evidence proxy vector (ut).
The method projects the teacher's original next-token correction onto ut to isolate intervention-aligned visual signals from linguistic priors and teacher-specific artifacts.
Training uses the reconstructed, student-anchored target as the primary supervision signal, supplemented by a weak regularizer from the privileged teacher.
Evaluated at 4B and 9B model scales across six fine-grained visual benchmarks, VAD outperformed both direct privileged-view distillation and visual-advantage weighting.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables multimodal student models to learn precise visual capabilities rather than inheriting ungrounded language priors or teacher-specific noise during knowledge distillation.

papers.title: AI systems and the reproduction of (standard) language ideologies in World Englishes

summary.tldr: This paper analyzes how AI systems reproduce dominant standard language ideologies that favor Inner Circle norms and marginalize Global South Englishes across training data, design protocols, evaluation benchmarks, and user feedback.
key_points: AI technologies reinforce standard language ideologies across model training data, design protocols, evaluation benchmarks, user feedback, and public discourse.
The public controversy around AI-sounding vocabulary (e.g., the word 'delve') demonstrates how Global North speakers police the English language norms of Global South users.

Generative AI exhibits a 'standardisation paradox,' simultaneously homogenizing English via standard form privileging and pluralizing it through broad training corpora and Global South annotation work.
Non-dominant World Englishes are increasingly and unfairly conflated with AI-generated speech.
summary.why_it_matters: Unexamined algorithmic bias toward standard Inner Circle norms leads to the marginalization and delegitimization of non-dominant Global South Englishes in automated systems.

papers.title: Lightning OPD 2.0: Mitigating Style Bias in Cross-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Large Reasoning Models

summary.tldr: Lightning OPD 2.0 introduces cross-fitted style residualization to remove style-token bias in cross-teacher on-policy distillation, eliminating the need for teacher consistency between SFT data generation and distillation teachers.
key_points: Identifies that cross-teacher OPD performance drops due to style bias from differences in wording, formatting, and reasoning cadence between non-identical SFT and distillation teachers.
Uses rollout-level cross-fitting to estimate style-token bias as a recurring residual component and subtracts it before constructing token-level OPD updates.
Achieves 82.4% on AIME 2024 and 63.0% on LiveCodeBench v5 starting from the Klear-Reasoner-8B-SFT base model.
Outperforms the original Lightning OPD in cross-teacher scenarios across mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows developers to independently select the optimal models for SFT data generation and distillation without requiring teacher consistency or sacrificing reasoning performance.

papers.title: Fidelity Is Not Safety: Gently-Compressed LLMs Pass Every Data-Free Quality Guard Yet Invent Procedure Steps in Agentic Execution

summary.tldr: Gently-compressed LLMs that pass standard perplexity, MMLU, and data-free representation fidelity guards still invent unauthorized SOP procedure steps during agentic execution due to coherent compression errors.
key_points: The step-invention behavior is operator-specific: coherent low-rank (SVD) truncation induces it, whereas magnitude pruning matched to the same perplexity does not.
The failures are governed by the product of compression error coherence and error rate, rather than the raw magnitude of damage.
Compressed weights that pass paired data-free output-fidelity tests under random probes consistently fail the invented-step canary across three model architectures.
The authors introduce a data-free two-axis screening statistic (coherent-fraction and error-rate) with fixed cross-architecture thresholds to flag failing low-rank builds.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard data-free quality and fidelity guards are insufficient to certify agent safety, requiring operators to specifically screen low-rank compressed models for error coherence before agentic deployment.

papers.title: Where and When to Commit: Candidate-Aware Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: LATCH introduces candidate-aware decoding for diffusion language models by separating global termination verification from local block acceleration.
key_points: Confidence-Verified Commit (CVC) controls sequence termination by checking confidence and argmax stability over dynamically extracted candidate spans via a task-specific parser.
Block-Wise Early Commit (BWEC) accelerates decoding locally by applying cheaper rules to non-final blocks while keeping the final block under CVC.
LATCH is prompt-anchor-free and format-aware, requiring no suffix-prompt construction.

Evaluated on 11 tasks with LLaDA and Dream models, LATCH achieves 9.3-17.8x TPS speedups on short-answer tasks and 2.0-3.3x on long-reasoning tasks within 2.0 percentage points of full-decoding accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables significant inference speedups in diffusion language models without requiring retraining or sacrificing generation accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

papers.title: RRM: Experience-Driven Reflective Retrieval Memory for Long-Horizon Multimodal Reasoning

summary.tldr: Reflective Retrieval Memory (RRM) improves long-horizon multimodal reasoning by adding a reflective experience memory that distills and reuses successful retrieval strategies across tasks.
key_points: Augments an entity-centric multimodal memory graph with reflective experience memory containing procedural retrieval knowledge distilled from past trajectories.
Converts retrieved past experiences into query-level search guidance while keeping answer generation strictly conditioned on factual evidence from the current video.
Implements a memory lifecycle management mechanism that prunes noise and redundancy using temporal decay, usage frequency, and reuse feedback.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on long-video multimodal benchmarks including M3-Bench-Robot, M3-Bench-Web, and Video-MME-Long.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-term multimodal agents to diagnose and fix retrieval failures by learning reusable search strategies rather than relying solely on static factual memory.

papers.title: Rethinking LLM-Judged Helpfulness as a Pedagogy Signal: A Pre-Registered Audit Across Tutor Models

summary.tldr: A pre-registered audit demonstrates that general-purpose LLM-judged helpfulness fails to distinguish direct answer-giving from pedagogical guidance in AI tutors, whereas targeted pedagogy rubrics and deterministic measures effectively separate tutor policies.
key_points: In a primary-base audit using Claude Opus 4.8 as judge, tutor policies showed no significant helpfulness difference but achieved complete rank-separation under a pedagogy rubric (Cliff's |δ|=0.10 vs. 1.0).

Helpfulness rank-orderings reversed between judges (Claude Opus 4.8 vs. GPT-5.6 Sol) on two of three tutor bases across 1,179 confirmatory turns, while pedagogy contrast directions remained consistent.
A seven-policy Opus ablation spanned a 2.3-point range in mean judged pedagogy while remaining constrained within a narrow 0.25-point helpfulness band.
Deterministic detectors confirmed that answer-revealing tutor turns directly lead to decreased next-turn independent work by students across all bases.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating educational LLMs with standard helpfulness rubrics obscures actual teaching quality and answer leakage, necessitating the use of specialized pedagogical rubrics and deterministic process metrics.

papers.title: Challenges in annotations by humans and LLMs: A case study of evaluative language

summary.tldr: A study compares linguists in training, an expert linguist, and LLMs on sentence-level Appraisal theory classification, showing fine-tuned LLMs achieve a 0.77 F1-score and closely align with expert annotations.
key_points: Evaluates the classification of Appraisal theory's Attitude subsystem (Affect, Judgement, Appreciation) using transcripts of English TED talks.
Tested three distinct prompts across three LLMs to determine optimal automatic classification performance.
Fine-tuning the best-performing LLM setup yielded an F1-score of 0.77.
LLM outputs agreed most strongly with the trained linguist, whereas linguists in training achieved low inter-annotator agreement.
summary.why_it_matters: Fine-tuned LLMs can match expert-level performance on highly subjective linguistic annotation tasks, offering a scalable alternative to training novice human annotators in digital humanities.

papers.title: GGC: Selective Query Correction for Reliable Text-to-SPARQL Generation

summary.tldr: The Generator-Gate-Corrector (GGC) framework improves Text-to-SPARQL reliability by selectively correcting high-risk LLM-generated queries using a gate mechanism, reducing unnecessary modifications and inference overhead.
key_points: GGC uses a three-stage pipeline: a Generator creates initial SPARQL queries, a Gate predicts if correction is needed, and a Corrector modifies only selected high-risk queries.
Selective correction prevents the degradation of initially correct queries and avoids unnecessary modifications.
Evaluated on MCQA, GGC increased query-level accuracy from 90.23% to 98.33%.
Compared to correcting all generated queries, GGC reduced inference overhead by 45%.
Ablation studies confirmed the Gate's robustness across thresholds and highlighted that Corrector training data composition impacts stability and effectiveness.
summary.why_it_matters: Selective correction enables higher accuracy and efficiency in Text-to-SPARQL systems by minimizing computational overhead and avoiding the degradation of valid queries.

papers.title: LEEPS: Latent-Guided Explore-Exploit Prompt Sampling for Efficient RLVR in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: LEEPS is a pre-rollout prompt sampler for RLVR that adaptively balances exploration and exploitation using representation-space neighbors to reduce wasteful rollouts in LLM training.
key_points: Partitions prompt candidates into exploit and explore portfolios, adaptively allocating rollout budget based on recent non-trivial reward ratios.
Prioritizes uncertain prompts likely to yield non-zero reward variance by leveraging representation-space neighbors and historical rollout outcomes without extra rollouts.
Outperforms baselines on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks with relative gains of 2.6% on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and 3.7% on Qwen2.5-Math-7B, while also improving OOD general-reasoning scores.
Introduces minimal computational latency, adding roughly 2 seconds of online sampling overhead per training step.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the computational efficiency and convergence speed of RLVR by preventing generation budget waste on uninformative prompts with identical rollout rewards.

papers.title: IFHierBench: Hierarchical Instruction Following for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: IFHierBench is a new benchmark featuring 600 prompts across four constraint-tree depths and 35 constraints to evaluate how LLMs follow hierarchical, scoped output constraints verified by deterministic checkers.
key_points: Evaluates hierarchical instruction following across four constraint-tree depths using 600 prompts and 35 distinct constraints.
Utilizes deterministic checkers to verify constraint satisfaction at the overall artifact, structural section, and nested field scopes.
Top proprietary and open-weight models score barely above 50% prompt-level accuracy, showing severe performance degradation as constraint depth increases.
summary.why_it_matters: Current LLMs struggle with multi-layered prompt instructions, highlighting the need for training methods that optimize constraint adherence at finer, nested granularities.

papers.title: AutoSupervision: Closing the Feedback Loop in Scientific Workflows with Grounded Revision Verification

summary.tldr: AutoSupervision introduces a framework and dataset to evaluate whether LLMs can verify that scientific paper revisions genuinely address reviewer concerns using grounded manuscript evidence.
key_points: Constructed from 56,000 Nature Communications articles and associated peer-review records.
Tasks require models to characterize reviewer concerns, determine if they are addressed, and identify supporting manuscript evidence.
GPT-5.5 achieved a 0.754 score in characterizing reviewer concerns.
Evidence-based verification proved to be the primary performance bottleneck, peaking at a score of 0.501.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a benchmark for automated peer-review workflows, highlighting that while LLMs can comprehend reviewer feedback, they still struggle to verify actual manuscript revisions against provided evidence.

papers.title: Gradient-free Task-Conditioned Retrieval for On-Device In-Context Learning

summary.tldr: Conditional Retrieval Alignment (CoRA) is a gradient-free framework that converts frozen encoders into task-conditioned retrievers using closed-form ridge regression, low-rank factorization, and an exact two-pass streaming construction for on-device in-context learning.
key_points: Uses closed-form ridge regression to align candidate input representations to an output-derived conditioning space constructed from candidate memory.
Applies low-rank factorization to yield an optimal low-rank compression basis, requiring candidate outputs only during offline indexing while query time uses only the input.
Features an exact two-pass streaming construction that avoids materializing the full fitted matrix in memory.
Extends to multimodal exemplar retrieval by embedding visual representations into the conditioning and retrieval spaces.
Validated across ten text and four multimodal benchmarks using Llama-3.2-1B, MobileLLM-Pro, OpenFlamingo-3B, and Qwen3.5-2B, including deployment on a Raspberry Pi 5.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables effective task-conditioned demonstration retrieval for on-device small language models without requiring retriever fine-tuning, backpropagation, or expensive target-model inference calls.

papers.title: Piggybacking on Perception: Stealthy Concurrent Audio Prompt Injections against Multimodal LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced stealthy concurrent audio prompt injection attacks that piggyback malicious instructions onto user speech, evaluated them using a new benchmark, and developed the Cascaded Audio Decoupling and Verification (CADV) defense.
key_points: Introduces instruction augmentation and scenario concealment techniques allowing malicious audio instructions to hide within background environmental noise during user speech.
Establishes AudioAgentSecurity, a benchmark covering 8 real-world task scenarios and 10 attack patterns to evaluate multimodal LLM agents.
Achieves a 69.10% average Attack Success Rate (ASR) against Gemini 3 Pro and demonstrates real-world viability on the Doubao AI Smartphone.
Proposes CADV, a defense using acoustic source separation and cross-modal consistency analysis that detects audio injections with over 90% success.
summary.why_it_matters: Audio-driven multimodal LLM agents can be covertly hijacked through ambient background noise, necessitating acoustic-level defenses like CADV alongside prompt-level safeguards.

papers.title: Agent Harness Distillation: Inference-Time Harness Extraction and Exploitation in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: Agent Harness Distillation (AHD) extracts proprietary inference-time multi-agent harnesses from black-box LLM systems through a two-stage extraction and refinement process.
key_points: Formalizes inference-time harness extraction as a novel security problem targeting intellectual property leakage in autonomous multi-agent systems (AMAS).
Uses a pre-distillation stage to infer harness behaviors from target agent responses and construct an initial harness.
Uses a post-distillation stage to iteratively refine and align the extracted harness with the target agent's behavioral patterns.
Proposes a deception-based defense mechanism that lowers extraction success while maintaining the target agent's utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals that dynamic, hard-to-engineer multi-agent coordination logic can be stolen via black-box querying, threatening the commercial IP of LLM-based agent systems.

papers.title: Safeguards Based on Copyable Context Cannot Provide Reliable Safety for LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers proved that LLM safeguards relying on copyable context face a mathematical safety trilemma where Useful Capability, Reliable Safety, and Open Access cannot simultaneously coexist without establishing a worst-case floor on attacker assistance.
key_points: LLM safeguards fail on dual-use tasks because copyable context allows attackers to perfectly imitate benign user requests and interaction histories.
Mathematical modeling proves an exact worst-case floor exists for attacker assistance if useful answers and open access are maintained under copyable evidence.
The study establishes a safety trilemma: developers cannot simultaneously achieve Useful Capability, Reliable Safety, and Open Access.
Incorporating trusted credentials introduces hard-to-copy information about actual downstream use, which is required to eliminate the assistance floor.
summary.why_it_matters: Open-access LLMs providing dual-use capabilities cannot be reliably secured using context-based safeguards alone, requiring a shift toward non-copyable trusted access credentials for safety.

papers.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball

summary.tldr: PAC-MAN combines control barrier functions, reinforcement learning, and an adversarial motion prior to enable zero-shot humanoid dodgeball evasion using only onboard ego-vision.
key_points: Uses a head-mounted camera with segmentation-masked depth for perception during deployment, paired with link-level control barrier function (CBF) guidance during training.
Utilizes an adversarial motion prior to regularize the humanoid robot's evasive reflexes.
Joint-CBF achieves optimal performance with precise ball states but degrades under fixed-camera setups, whereas Link-CBF handles imperfect perception better.
Achieved a 95% dodge success rate during zero-shot real-world deployment on the Unitree G1 humanoid using semantic segmentation.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that lightweight control barrier techniques combined with onboard vision allow physical humanoids to execute rapid, dynamic whole-body collision avoidance without relying on external motion capture systems.

papers.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems

summary.tldr: APO is an unsupervised alignment framework for 3D atomic structure prediction that eliminates the need for ground-truth reference structures by adapting group-relative policy optimization with a dual-reward mechanism.
key_points: Adapts group-relative policy optimization to 3D atomic flow-matching models without using supervised preference learning or experimental labels.
Utilizes an intrinsic reward based on eigen-decomposition of sample similarities to reinforce dominant latent structural modes within sampled groups.
Incorporates a physical reward function that enforces thermodynamic stability to help models self-correct toward plausible configurations.
Straightens probability paths during generation, which improves overall inference efficiency.
Outperforms fully supervised baselines like FlowDPO in match rates and structural fidelity for crystal and antibody structure prediction.
summary.why_it_matters: APO enables high-accuracy 3D structural modeling and faster inference for novel crystals and proteins where experimental ground-truth coordinates are unavailable or costly to obtain.

papers.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers

summary.tldr: MixFrag is a mixed-precision post-training quantization framework for Vision Transformers that allocates component-level bit-widths by measuring output distribution divergence and solving a Multiple-Choice Knapsack Problem.
key_points: Quantization fragility is estimated at the component level by measuring KL divergence between full-precision and isolated quantized output distributions on a calibration set.
Precision assignment is formulated and solved as a Multiple-Choice Knapsack Problem (MCKP) to adaptively allocate layer-wise bit-widths under a target memory budget.
Evaluations on COCO object detection and instance segmentation show up to a 9.6 AP improvement over existing mixed-precision PTQ methods under the MP3/MP3 setting.
Validated on ImageNet-1K classification across multiple Vision Transformer architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate deployment of Vision Transformers on resource-constrained hardware by optimally matching bit-precision to the sensitivity of individual model components without full retraining.

papers.title: Same Graph Cross-Task Transfer in GNNs: Protocols and Predictors

summary.tldr: Researchers formalized same-graph cross-task transfer between node classification and link prediction, introducing a leakage-free protocol and the CoTask Score to predict and optimize representation transfer.
key_points: Establishes a leakage-free protocol using fixed node/edge splits, a shared message-passing graph excluding evaluated edges, and fixed negatives for link prediction (LP).
Identifies directional asymmetry across GCN, GraphSAGE, and GPS backbones: NC-to-LP transfer consistently improves performance on homophilic graphs, whereas LP-to-NC transfer is fragile.
Shows LP-to-NC transfer succeeds primarily in structure-dominant regimes where LP is easy and NC is unsaturated, effectively serving as structural pretraining.
Introduces the CoTask Score (CTS) to evaluate joint NC and LP utility for a shared encoder, using dataset homophily to guide transfer strategies and avoid negative transfer.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides standardized protocols and predictable metrics to safely reuse supervision across multiple tasks on a single graph without performance degradation.

papers.title: Oracle-Budgeted Molecular Optimization with Short-Term Graph Memory

summary.tldr: The authors introduce a plug-in short-term graph memory module that uses an online GNN surrogate to pre-screen generated molecules, improving candidate selection under tight, fixed oracle budgets.
key_points: Maintains an online graph neural network (GNN) surrogate to pre-screen candidate pools before committing oracle calls.
Preserves the underlying generator architecture and native update rules without requiring structural modifications.
Consistently improves mean top-10 scores across four tested fragment-based generators at a 1,000-oracle-call budget without incurring extra oracle costs.
Demonstrates that optimization benefits depend on the backbone generator's search breadth and native capacity to exploit oracle feedback.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a plug-and-play method to increase the yield of high-performing molecules from expensive computational or experimental oracle evaluations without altering existing generation algorithms.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus

summary.tldr: A semi-supervised ensemble consensus training method enhances graph neural network accuracy, model robustness, and calibration for molecular property prediction without relying on label-preserving data augmentations.
key_points: Bypasses the need for complex, label-preserving molecular data augmentations by using an ensemble consensus objective on unlabeled data.
Individual models trained with this semi-supervised consensus objective consistently outperform full ensembles trained via traditional supervised methods.
Demonstrates an effect similar to knowledge distillation while simultaneously reducing model calibration error across diverse molecular datasets and GNN architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables high-accuracy, well-calibrated molecular property predictions using abundant unlabeled data, bypassing the challenge of creating domain-specific graph augmentations.

papers.title: Search Strategies for Optimal Classification and Regression Trees

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced a unified algorithmic framework for Optimal Decision Trees (ODTs) to evaluate 18 search strategies, achieving an order of magnitude faster regression runtime and improved anytime classification performance.
key_points: Introduces a general, unified algorithmic framework that instantiates existing ODT search strategies and enables new ones.
Empirically evaluates and compares the performance impact of 18 distinct search strategies across classification and regression tasks.
Demonstrates an order-of-magnitude runtime improvement for regression and superior anytime performance for classification compared to state-of-the-art methods.
summary.why_it_matters: The framework isolates which search strategies best overcome the scalability limits of globally optimal decision trees, enabling faster and more accurate interpretable modeling.

authors: Jacobus G. M. van der Linden

papers.title: On a joint simultaneous learning of relevant feature subsets and subspaces in regression-like problems

summary.tldr: Entropy-Optimal Manifold Regression (EOMR) extends EOMC to jointly identify relevant feature subsets and subspaces in nonlinear, nonstationary regression problems with linear iteration and memory complexity.
key_points: EOMR scales linearly in both iteration and memory complexities while addressing nonstationary and nonlinear regression.
Outperformed gradient boosted random forests, deep neural networks, and TabPFN v.03 by orders of magnitude in root mean squared prediction error on chaotic and fluid dynamics benchmarks.
Tested on Lorenz-96 chaotic systems (forcing parameters F=8 and F=12) and edge tokamak plasma data from the Hasegawa-Wakatani model.
Distilled the Hasegawa-Wakatani leading Essential Orthogonal Function (EOF) dynamics into a linear, causal, weakly-stationary autoregressive process using only 8 parameters.
summary.why_it_matters: EOMR enables highly accurate, lower-complexity predictive modeling for challenging chaotic and fluid dynamics systems compared to current deep learning and tree-based tools.

papers.title: Beyond Sentiment: Structured Information Extraction from Financial News

summary.tldr: A new framework uses LLaMA-3.1-70B to extract six orthogonal semantic dimensions from financial news, proving that combining structured semantic features with FinBERT sentiment significantly improves stock return prediction over sentiment alone.
key_points: LLaMA-3.1-70B extracts six semantic dimensions (event type, impact scope, temporal horizon, confidence, etc.) from news, exhibiting a 53.5% systematic disagreement rate with traditional sentiment analysis.
FinBERT sentiment exhibits a non-linear relationship with stock returns, achieving an F1 score of 0.576 under non-linear models versus 0.230 under linear models.
Combining FinBERT sentiment with LLM-extracted structural features yields a top F1 score of 0.600 (p < 0.0001) across 41,618 news-stock pairs from the FNSPID dataset.
Ablation studies show non-sentiment structural dimensions independently add +0.019 F1, with balanced feature importance across all six dimensions (14-21%).
summary.why_it_matters: Compressing financial text into a single sentiment score loses critical predictive signal, which can be recovered by combining sentiment with multi-dimensional LLM extraction.

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Execute Parent Orders?

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced PACE, a hierarchical LLM framework for parent-order execution that outperforms traditional and learning-based baselines without requiring task-specific training or explicit market assumptions.
key_points: Presents PACE (Plan-Ahead Controlled Execution), a hierarchical framework dividing order execution into long-horizon planning and short-horizon execution.
Eliminates the need for explicit market assumptions and task-specific training in algorithmic trading execution.
Outperformed TWAP, Almgren-Chriss, and learning-based baselines by 0.65 bps on Shenzhen Stock Exchange Level-1 data.
Behavioral analysis indicates LLMs trade earlier than humans and achieve better performance when model confidence is high.
summary.why_it_matters: This study demonstrates that LLMs can effectively execute complex trading orders out-of-the-box, expanding financial LLM applications from trade selection to execution optimization.

papers.title: FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework

summary.tldr: FinanceHarness is an end-to-end framework and verifiable benchmark (FinanceGym) designed to execute and evaluate autonomous, point-in-time financial deep research without future information leakage.
key_points: FinanceHarness automates environment construction, data ingestion, agent execution, and reward modeling using finance-oriented tools and practitioner workflows.
FinanceGym introduces thesis-driven research questions evaluated against point-in-time rubrics combining pre-cutoff and post-cutoff criteria.
Leading LLMs and agents score under 40% on FinanceGym rubrics despite the benchmark achieving an 82% pass rate during professional expert validation.
Using the same open-weight backbone, FinanceHarness increases the overall rubric score from 25.3% to 32.4% over baseline agent implementations.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized, leak-free framework and benchmark to advance autonomous AI agents from writing general reports to conducting rigorous, domain-specific financial research.

papers.title: Beyond Borrowed Histories: Person-Aligned User Simulation for Interactive Role-Playing Evaluation

summary.tldr: PALATE is a role-playing agent benchmark that replaces fixed dialogue histories and generic rubrics with five per-user simulators and personalized evaluation rubrics across 300 character profiles.
key_points: Identifies two core flaws in existing RPA benchmarks: dependency on static dialogue histories and mismatched, unaligned general rubrics.
Introduces PALATE using five per-user simulators that conduct multi-turn, free-form conversations across a pool of 300 character profiles.
Constructs personalized rubrics alongside a general quality rubric, demonstrating higher agreement with human judgments on held-out annotated data.
Evaluates 16 candidate RPAs by measuring generic turn quality, long-horizon session capability, and per-user experience without collapsing scores into a single aggregate ranking.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables more accurate, human-aligned benchmarking of role-playing agents by capturing user-specific satisfaction and dynamic multi-turn interactions rather than static histories.

papers.title: Semantic-Aligned Structural Abstraction for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

summary.tldr: SentiLLM introduces a Semantic-Aligned Structural Abstraction framework that discretizes continuous non-verbal modalities into compact, text-like tokens using a Dual-Stream Salience-Context Calibration Mechanism for multimodal sentiment analysis.
key_points: Exploits structural isomorphism between non-verbal modalities and natural language sequences to convert audio and visual features into LLM-understandable tokens.
Features a Dual-Stream Salience-Context Calibration Mechanism that separates features into a text-guided focus stream for salient sentiment shifts and an ambient stream for background states.
Acts as a plug-and-play module that requires tuning only a small number of trainable parameters.
Evaluated across four multimodal sentiment datasets: MOSI, MOSEI, CH-SIMS, and CH-SIMS v2.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables Large Language Models to process complex affective non-verbal signals using a parameter-efficient, plug-and-play architecture without relying on low-level superficial feature mapping.

papers.title: Old Tricks, New Models: How Simple Image Transformations Break Modern AI-based Content Moderation

summary.tldr: Commercial foundation-model-based image moderation APIs remain vulnerable to simple, model-agnostic, gradient-free transformations like color inversion and grayscale conversion that bypass safety filters while keeping harmful content recognizable to humans.
key_points: A black-box evaluation of three commercial image-moderation services revealed that simple, inexpensive image transformations bypass safety filters without requiring gradients, surrogate models, or target system knowledge.
Fixed, non-adversarial transformations such as color inversion and grayscale conversion consistently trigger unsafe-to-safe decision changes.
Robustness varies significantly by category, with multimodal content and self-harm categories demonstrating the highest vulnerability to evasion.
Foundation-model-based moderation APIs fail to provide a reliable standalone security boundary.
summary.why_it_matters: Replacing conventional moderation classifiers with large foundation models does not automatically guarantee robustness against basic visual evasion tactics, necessitating a layered moderation approach.

papers.title: Temporal Poisoning: Clean-Label Backdoors via Event Redistribution in SNNs

summary.tldr: A novel clean-label temporal poisoning backdoor attack against Spiking Neural Networks alters event stream timestamps without changing target labels or overall per-pixel event counts, achieving up to 100% Attack Success Rate.
key_points: Applies a fixed timestamp transformation to target-class training streams without altering original labels.
Preserves per-pixel, per-polarity event counts exactly, making poisoned and clean samples identical under time-collapsed rate aggregation.
Achieves an Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 1.00 on convolutional and transformer-based SNN architectures across three neuromorphic datasets.
Renders defenses that collapse the time axis ineffective by construction, though a model-free detector tracking per-step event mass successfully detects the transformation.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that Spiking Neural Networks are vulnerable to stealthy, clean-label backdoor attacks that bypass traditional rate-based defenses by exploiting the temporal dimension of neuromorphic event data.

papers.title: Driving up Inference Energy on SNNs: Per-Sample and Universal Sponge Attacks

summary.tldr: Researchers developed per-sample and universal sponge attacks targeting native event-based Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), significantly inflating synaptic operations and energy consumption while maintaining model accuracy above 98%.
key_points: Per-sample attacks use gradient-based optimization to craft adversarial spike trains, increasing SynOps by 1.5-2.6x on NMNIST, SHD, and IBM DVS Gesture datasets.
Universal attacks apply a single offline-computed binary perturbation via XOR to all inputs, increasing SynOps by 1.09-1.24x without requiring per-input optimization.
Energy mapping onto Loihi-1 neuromorphic hardware demonstrated per-inference overheads ranging from 14 μJ to 13.24 mJ.
summary.why_it_matters: These attacks demonstrate that event-based SNNs in battery-powered edge devices can be targeted to drain power rapidly without triggering accuracy-based detection mechanisms.

papers.title: Don't Trust the AI Ecosystem: Analyzing Privacy Leakage in Compromised Open-Source Components

summary.tldr: GradLock is a training-time injection attack that uses stateless deterministic indexing and dynamic gradient locking to stealthily embed pixel-perfect training data directly into open-source model parameters for rapid extraction.
key_points: GradLock uses stateless deterministic indexing to create isolated data vaults and dynamic gradient locking to prevent payload degradation during training.
Achieves near-lossless reconstruction (SSIM ~ 1.0) and instant extraction times under 1.0 second on MNIST, Imagenette, and CelebA datasets.
Demonstrates robustness against post-training deployment optimizations such as quantization, pruning, and fine-tuning.
A user deployment study showed 93.3% of participants failed to detect the injected malicious logic within the supply chain context.
summary.why_it_matters: This vulnerability highlights a critical supply chain risk where compromised open-source AI components can completely leak sensitive training data while evading standard detection methods.

papers.title: CHARGE: Leveraging CWE Hierarchies for Hardware Security SystemVerilog Assertion Generation

summary.tldr: CHARGE is an automated framework that leverages CWE hierarchies and LLMs to identify security assets and generate SystemVerilog Assertions for unverified RTL modules without trusted specifications.
key_points: Uses CWE entries' hierarchical structures combined with GPT-4.1 to infer expected security behaviors directly from unverified RTL modules.
Evaluated on Hack@DAC18, 19, and 21 open-source SoCs, detecting 27 out of 42 known hardware security bugs.
Achieves an 89% execution rate in Cadence JasperGold FPV with 92.2% non-vacuous assertions on the Hack@DAC21 OpenPiton SoC.
Outperformed manually written open-source properties by fixing errors in three existing bug properties and discovering a previously unidentified bug in OpenPiton.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the dependency on trusted design specifications for hardware formal verification, reducing manual engineering effort while uncovering bugs missed by human-written assertions.

papers.title: Revisiting the Adversarial Robustness of Graph-Based Traffic Forecasting

summary.tldr: Researchers re-evaluated graph-based traffic forecasting security using a localized, physics-aware attack model and proposed a learned physics-informed detector that outperforms standard adversarial training across multiple benchmarks with near-zero clean performance cost.
key_points: Prior robustness evaluations rely on unrealistic, untargeted, norm-bounded threat models that fail to capture localized, physics-aware attacks designed to mimic real congestion on specific links.
The proposed physics-aware attack significantly increases target-link forecasting errors while leaving overall network-wide error metrics largely unchanged.
Standard adversarial training tuned for norm-bounded perturbations fails to defend against these structural, physics-aware manipulation techniques.

The proposed defense uses a learned physics-informed detector to pass features to a hardened forecaster, outperforming adversarial training on 13 of 15 model-dataset configurations and showing strong generalization to held-out attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that standard AI adversarial defenses fail against practical, domain-specific attacks on transportation infrastructure, requiring physics-informed detection to prevent targeted route manipulation.

papers.title: AnchorMark: Robust Diffusion Watermarking via Latent-Space Rotation Synchrony

summary.tldr: AnchorMark is a training-free, inversion-based diffusion watermarking method that leverages latent-space rotation synchrony and a central synchronization anchor to withstand spatial rotation and compound post-processing attacks.
key_points: Identifies Rotation Synchrony, where image-domain rotations match the rotation angle of the recovered initial latent space.
Embeds a synchronization anchor in the central region of the initial latent to estimate and correct rotation angles during watermark extraction.
Eliminates the need for a post-hoc image-domain embedding stage while maintaining native visual fidelity without model retraining.
Demonstrates significantly improved bit accuracy under rotation and combined lossy post-processing attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It restores spatial correspondence for latent-space decoding, rendering inversion-based diffusion watermarks resilient against rotation-based tampering without degrading image quality.

papers.title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: MANTA is a multi-agent framework that self-evolves its communication topology at inference time by applying bounded structural updates to agent roles, links, execution order, visibility, and validation pathways based on collaboration traces.
key_points: Initializes a task-conditioned topology from prior structural experience prior to task execution.
Monitors collaboration traces during deployment to trigger dynamic, bounded updates without changing the task interface or agent budget.
Modifies communication links, agent roles, execution sequencing, information visibility, and validation pathways dynamically.

Achieved a top average score of 74.0 across five benchmarks (spanning information seeking, tool use, planning, workflow execution, and math reasoning), outperforming the best baseline by 5.8 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that multi-agent systems can improve performance during inference by dynamically reconfiguring their own organizational architecture rather than relying on static or offline-optimized communication topologies.

papers.title: AI and Authenticity in Islamic Research: A Critical Evaluation of Generative AI Reliability, Hallucination, and Source Fidelity in Quranic, Hadith, and Fiqh Knowledge

summary.tldr: A multi-region study evaluated six generative AI models across fifty Islamic knowledge questions, revealing critical vulnerabilities in religious source verification, citation accuracy, and jurisprudential consistency.
key_points: Evaluated six leading generative AI systems using 50 open-ended questions spanning Quranic interpretation, Hadith, Fiqh, ethics, and Madhhab-sensitive topics.
Analyzed model outputs across domain accuracy, citation verification, hallucinations, uncertainty handling, source provenance, and geographical variation in the UK and Australia.
Findings indicate current models hallucinate and provide incomplete or unverifiable religious references and citations.
Systems demonstrate limitations in handling jurisprudential disagreements and Madhhab diversity consistently.
summary.why_it_matters: Current generative AI models are unsuitable as authoritative sources for religious rulings or scholarly Islamic research without human verification against authenticated primary sources.

papers.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models

summary.tldr: OSReward introduces a standardized benchmark for evaluating vision-language models as computer-use agent reward judges, revealing widespread leniency bias and proposing open OS-Shepherd models trained on OS-Shepherd-100K to provide low-cost, accurate verification.
key_points: OSReward evaluates VLM judges on multi-platform CUA trajectories, supplemented by OSReward-Hard for difficult cases and OSReward-Multi for fine-grained efficiency and alignment scoring.
Evaluation reveals state-of-the-art VLMs suffer from a systematic leniency bias that mislabels failed agent trajectories as successful.
To address performance and cost issues, the authors created OS-Shepherd-100K, an open corpus of reasoning-annotated trajectory judgments.
Using this corpus, the authors trained OS-Shepherd (9B and 35B) open reward models, matching commercial judges at 30-60% lower cost than frontier models.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, cost-effective, and reliable reinforcement learning and evaluation for computer-using agents without relying on expensive commercial VLM judges.

papers.title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks

summary.tldr: PAIChecker is a multi-agent system designed to detect PR-Issue misalignments in SWE-bench-like benchmarks using a three-phase verification workflow.
key_points: Analysis of SWE-bench Verified instances revealed that 13.6% contain PR-Issue misalignments across five patterns and eleven fine-grained scenarios.
PAIChecker operates via a three-phase architecture: pattern identification, cross-agent label synthesis, and code-level validation.
Evaluating PAIChecker on SWE-Gym and SWE-bench Multilingual yielded up to 92.12% and 91.67% binary accuracy across four LLM backbones.
summary.why_it_matters: Identifying PR-issue misalignments prevents flawed test oracles and inaccurate problem statements from corrupting LLM evaluation benchmarks.

papers.title: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs

summary.tldr: A systematic empirical study evaluates inference-time scaling dimensions for local computer-use agents on OSWorld, finding that additional compute yields diminishing returns and alters model failure modes rather than simply increasing success rates.
key_points: Evaluated local models (Qwen3-VL-8B/30B-A3B, UI-TARS-1.5-7B, and OpenCUA-7B) across contextual, temporal, structural, and parallel scaling dimensions on OSWorld.
Contextual scaling improves trajectory stability and accuracy, but gains saturate at higher token costs as failure modes shift from repetitive loops to premature false successes.
Temporal scaling reduces maximum-step stalls but fails to boost task success, as extended execution horizons tend to prolong erroneous trajectories rather than self-correct.
Structural decomposition in local two-stage agents creates planning and formatting overhead, which parallel scaling only partially mitigates at high computational costs.
summary.why_it_matters: Designing efficient local computer-use agents requires selective compute allocation and failure-aware control rather than naive inference-time scaling.

papers.title: On-Policy and Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces

summary.tldr: This thesis presents structured Bayesian methods for on-policy contextual bandits and differentiable pessimistic objectives for off-policy learning to address scalability issues in large action spaces.
key_points: Introduces meTS (mixed-effect Thompson sampling) and dTS (diffusion-inspired priors) to share information across actions and provide regret guarantees based on an effective action count.
Proposes sDM, a latent-variable structured direct method, demonstrating that optimization error often dominates estimation error in large action spaces.
Formulates concave, efficiently optimizable policy-weighted log-likelihood objectives for off-policy policy improvement.
Develops differentiable pessimistic methods using exponential smoothing and PAC-Bayesian bounds to manage bias-variance trade-offs in regularized importance-sampling estimators.
summary.why_it_matters: These methods reduce variance and improve sample efficiency when training interactive decision-making agents with massive action sets from online or logged data.

papers.title: ThreatForest: Multi-Agent Attack Tree Generation with Pluggable TTP Framework Mapping

summary.tldr: ThreatForest is a multi-agent system that converts source code repositories into structured, TTP-mapped attack trees and mitigations using orchestrated pipeline stages, deterministic verification gates, and pluggable threat framework mappings.
key_points: Decomposes threat modeling into five orchestrated stages (repo analysis, context refinement, threat generation, parallel attack-tree construction, report generation) with three human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
Uses a domain-specific sentence-transformer and cosine similarity to map attack steps to MITRE ATT&CK, CAPEC, and cloud-specific threat matrices.
Achieves 0.63-0.68 quality scores for threat statements, attack trees, and mitigations across seven domains, but drops to 0.29 for embedding-only TTP mapping.
Identifies the sentence-transformer encoder, rather than the multi-agent orchestration, as the primary accuracy bottleneck in TTP mapping.
summary.why_it_matters: It automates end-to-end cloud-native threat modeling directly from source code while isolating embedding accuracy as the key technical constraint for automated TTP mapping.

papers.title: MemSecBench: Tracking Agent Memory Poisoning from Persistence to Consequence and Repair

summary.tldr: MemSecBench is a new task-grounded benchmark evaluating agent memory poisoning and selective repair across a 7-checkpoint Write-Execute-Forget lifecycle in 24 runtime configurations.
key_points: Evaluates 310 cases across 48 contexts using a controlled Write-Execute-Forget protocol across seven lifecycle checkpoints.
Tests a 24-configuration matrix combining two agent harnesses, four memory backends, and three LLM backends.
Across all configurations, malicious memory persisted in 84.2% of cases, with the full Write-Execute attack chain succeeding in 50.3%.
Selective repair succeeded in 56.1% of poisoned cases, while memory system choices altered end-to-end attack success by up to 16.1 percentage points and repair rates by 41.3 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that choice of memory backend and agent architecture significantly affects vulnerability to long-term memory poisoning and the ability to selectively purge malicious instructions.

papers.title: What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation

summary.tldr: A new three-class detection framework identifies AI browser-automation agents with 100% recall using as few as two behavioral features, exposing a fundamental limitation in traditional binary human-vs-bot classifiers.
key_points: Binary human-vs-bot classifiers fail to represent AI agents, with an MLP and SAINT transformer misclassifying 39.1% and 34.5% of agent sessions as human, respectively.
Introducing an explicit agent class achieved a per-class agent F1 score of 1.000 across 30 runs, with zero misses across 22,990 evasion test sessions.
The primary detection signal stems from Playwright browser-automation artifacts—specifically the absence of raw pointer-move and wheel-delta streams produced by physical input devices.

summary.tldr: vLLM on Arm CPUs has been optimized through collaborations with PyTorch, oneDNN, and KleidiAI communities, resulting in improved usability, broader model support, and substantial performance gains.

infra.title: Parallel All the Way Down: Beyond Single-Token Generation with Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: vLLM and Speculators now support P-EAGLE, DFlash, and DSpark, three parallel drafting algorithms that generate entire blocks of candidate tokens concurrently, moving beyond sequential token generation in speculative decoding.
key_points: Traditional speculative decoding frameworks like EAGLE-3 use auto-regressive drafting, requiring a separate forward pass for each candidate token, introducing sequential latency.
Parallel drafting algorithms predict an entire candidate block of tokens concurrently in a single forward pass, decoupling proposal generation latency from the number of tokens speculated.

This architectural shift allows for larger, more expressive draft architectures without sequential latency penalties and simplifies parameter tuning by removing the dependency of drafting cost on block length.
P-EAGLE, DFlash, and DSpark combine parallel execution with deep verifier-state conditioning, building on the insight from EAGLE to generate draft tokens.
A shared challenge for parallel speculators is training, as they must perform next-K prediction at every token position along a training sequence.
summary.why_it_matters: This advancement significantly mitigates memory-bandwidth bottlenecks in LLM serving, leading to substantial inference speedups in production systems.
